project.name: cosmos-v2
project.description: Multi-tenant project- and program-management platform: boards (Kanban, Scrum, Backlog, Roadmap, Gantt), OKRs, RAID logs, SAFe program increments, document ingestion, and an in-app feedback portal with autonomous AI-driven delivery (Foreman daemon) — org-scoped with RBAC/ABAC access control. Next.js 16 + React 19 + Prisma 7/PostgreSQL.

nodes.languageNotes: Mocks only getAuthContext via vi.hoisted/vi.mock so RBAC can be driven while every query hits the real DB, letting BEFORE-INSERT hash-chain triggers fire on seeded rows.

nodes.name: engine.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, I/O-free work-role ABAC decision engine: DENY-only rules narrow the RBAC bitfield, with owner break-glass first, fail-closed handling of unresolvable conditions, and prototype-pollution-safe attribute paths.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately a pure synchronous function (no DB, no async) so the security-critical decision logic is exhaustively unit-testable; every invariant maps to a reviewed risk and a test.

nodes.name: evaluateAccess
nodes.summary: Pure access decision: owner break-glass first, then the bitfield check (fail-closed on unknown actions), then deny-precedence evaluation of rules referencing the action.

nodes.name: coerceRules
nodes.summary: Coerces stored JSON (bare array or { rules } wrapper) into well-formed AbacRule[], dropping malformed rules and conditions.

nodes.name: compare
nodes.summary: Operator comparison that coerces numeric strings for gt/gte/lt/lte so a deny cannot silently no-op on type mismatches.

nodes.name: resolveRelationship
nodes.summary: Resolves relationship predicates: owns_resource is computed purely from resource attributes; DB-backed predicates read from the pre-resolved map or return unresolvable.

nodes.name: evalCondition
nodes.summary: Evaluates one condition to true/false/unresolvable, treating operand/operator type mismatches as unresolvable so denies fail closed.

nodes.name: isValidCondition
nodes.summary: Type guard requiring a known relationship or a non-empty attr with a known operator.

nodes.name: isAbacRule
nodes.summary: Type guard validating rule shape (effect, string actions, valid conditions) before rules reach the pure engine.

nodes.name: require-access.ts
nodes.summary: Resource-aware authorization gate layering ABAC on the RBAC bitfield: resolves only the DB-backed relationship predicates the relevant rules actually use, defers to the pure engine, and throws ForbiddenError on denial.

nodes.name: requireAccess
nodes.summary: Async gate that pre-resolves in_project only when a relevant rule needs it (leaving it unresolved on error so denies fail closed) and throws ForbiddenError when evaluateAccess denies.

nodes.name: isActorInProject

nodes.name: resolveAuth

nodes.name: listMatchCandidates

nodes.name: excludeTransaction

nodes.name: postPayRun

nodes.summary: Zod schemas for employee creation/update and pay-run input used by the payroll API routes.

nodes.name: contract.ts

nodes.name: generateContractPdf

nodes.name: revoke-core.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the Google token revocation core, exercising URL construction, success classification, and revokeOneToken behavior against the fake Google fetch implementation.

nodes.name: revoke-core.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free helpers for revoking Google OAuth refresh tokens: builds revoke-endpoint URLs, classifies revocation outcomes, and performs a single token revocation with injectable fetch.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses an injectable fetch implementation so the same core runs against real Google or a fake endpoint in tests.

nodes.name: isRevokeSuccess
nodes.summary: Classifies a revocation result as success, treating both revoked and already-invalid tokens as successful outcomes.

nodes.name: buildRevokeUrl
nodes.summary: Builds the Google token revocation endpoint URL with the refresh token URL-encoded as a query parameter.

nodes.name: revokeOneToken
nodes.summary: Revokes a single refresh token via the provided fetch implementation, mapping HTTP status and response body (including invalid_token bodies) into a typed revocation result.

nodes.name: revoke-fake-google.ts
nodes.summary: File-state-backed fake of Google's token revoke endpoint that records revoked token hashes to a JSON state file, used for cutover rehearsals and tests.

nodes.name: load
nodes.summary: Loads the fake-revocation state file from disk, returning an empty default state when the file does not exist or cannot be parsed.

nodes.name: makeFakeGoogleFetch
nodes.summary: Creates a fetch-compatible function simulating Google's revoke endpoint: extracts the token from the URL, records its SHA-256 hash in the state file, and returns Google-shaped responses.

nodes.name: revoke-google-tokens.mjs
nodes.summary: Cutover CLI that unseals stored Google refresh tokens from the database and revokes them at Google (or the fake endpoint), producing a per-credential JSON report.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses CLI flags (org id, mode, state path) into an options object, failing fast on unknown arguments.

nodes.name: resolveFetch
nodes.summary: Selects the fetch implementation for revocation: the fake Google fetch in rehearsal mode (via makeFakeGoogleFetch) or real global fetch for live revocation.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Validates arguments, loads sealed Google credentials for the target org from Postgres, opens each secret with openSecret, revokes tokens via revokeOneToken, and emits a JSON summary report with a non-zero exit on failures.

nodes.name: rotate-vault-key.mjs
nodes.summary: Vault key rotation script that re-wraps every sealed database column from the previous key to the active key, verifying key-id (kid) consistency and reporting a rotation summary.
nodes.languageNotes: Rotation is column-driven: each sealed column is scanned, non-active-kid values are re-wrapped with rewrapSecret, and the script aborts on unsealed or unknown-kid values.

nodes.name: rotateColumn
nodes.summary: Scans one sealed table column, validates each value is sealed with a known kid, re-wraps non-active-kid values via rewrapSecret, and writes them back with parameterized updates.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Validates required env vars, resolves the active key id, iterates all configured sealed columns through rotateColumn, and prints a JSON rotation summary with appropriate exit codes.

nodes.name: seal-google-tokens.mjs
nodes.summary: One-time migration script that vault-seals plaintext Google refresh tokens into encrypted credential rows, resolving each user's primary org and clearing the plaintext column afterwards.

nodes.name: upsertSealedCredential
nodes.summary: Inserts or updates a sealed Google credential row for a user/org pair using raw SQL upsert queries.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Loads users with plaintext refresh tokens, resolves each primary org, seals the token JSON with sealSecret, upserts the sealed credential, nulls the plaintext column, and prints a JSON summary.

nodes.name: route.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the logout route, asserting that session deletion and cookie clearing behave correctly for requests with and without session cookies.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: GET logout entry point delegating to clearSession.

nodes.summary: Handles the Microsoft OAuth callback: state validation, code exchange via exchangeMicrosoftCode, profile fetch, allowlist matching over candidate emails, user provisioning, and session cookie issuance.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Initiates Microsoft OAuth login when the provider is configured: rate-limits, sets a state cookie, and redirects to the Microsoft authorize URL.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Checks provider configuration, rate-limits, generates a random state, and redirects to the Microsoft authorization URL with the state cookie set.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Tiny status endpoint reporting whether Microsoft login is configured, based on the stored provider configuration.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Returns the Microsoft provider status as JSON via getProviderStatus.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: First-login password change endpoint: validates the sealed first-login cookie, verifies the temporary password, enforces the password policy, stores the new hash, and advances the flow to MFA setup or session issuance.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Rate-limits, loads the first-login user from the cookie, validates and rehashes the new password, then either seals an MFA-pending cookie, continues the first-login flow, or finishes the login with a session.

nodes.name: first-login-flow.test.ts
nodes.summary: Integration test covering the entire first-login flow across login, forced password change, TOTP MFA setup, and MFA enrollment, including a local base32/TOTP generator to produce valid codes.

nodes.name: totpNow
nodes.summary: Test helper computing the current 6-digit TOTP code from a base32 secret using HMAC-SHA1, mirroring the server-side TOTP algorithm.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: First-login MFA enrollment endpoint: verifies a TOTP code against the vault-sealed pending secret, activates MFA with hashed recovery codes, and completes the password login session.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Rate-limits, loads the first-login user, verifies the submitted TOTP code via verifyTotp against the opened sealed secret, persists MFA activation with generated recovery codes, and finishes the login.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: First-login MFA setup endpoint that generates a new TOTP secret, seals it into the user record, and returns the otpauth provisioning URI for authenticator apps.

nodes.summary: Validates the first-login cookie and flow state, generates a TOTP secret, stores it sealed via sealSecret, and responds with the totpUri for enrollment.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Password login endpoint: rate-limits by IP and email, verifies the password hash with timing-safe fallback, enforces gov-SSO blocking, and branches into the first-login flow, MFA challenge, or immediate session issuance.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Validates credentials with verifyPassword, checks SSO enforcement, and depending on user state sets a sealed first-login cookie, a sealed MFA-pending cookie, or finishes the login via finishPasswordLogin.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: MFA verification endpoint that opens the sealed MFA-pending cookie, verifies a TOTP code or consumes a recovery code, and completes the password login with a session.

nodes.summary: Decrypts and expires the MFA-pending cookie, rate-limits per user, verifies TOTP via verifyTotp or a recovery code via consumeRecoveryCode, and finishes the login on success.

nodes.summary: Password reset request endpoint: rate-limits by IP and email, silently no-ops for unknown accounts, creates a fingerprinted reset token, and emails a reset link branded for the user's organization.

nodes.name: reset-flow.test.ts

nodes.summary: Starts an org-scoped OIDC SSO login: resolves the org's IdP configuration, generates PKCE verifier/challenge, state, and nonce, stores them in a transaction cookie, and redirects to the IdP authorization URL.

nodes.summary: Rate-limits, looks up the organization and IdP connection, discovers OIDC config via getOidcConfig, builds the authorization URL with PKCE parameters, and sets the SSO transaction cookie before redirecting.

nodes.summary: Public status endpoint reporting whether SSO is configured and enforced for an organization slug, with rate limiting.

nodes.name: claude-oauth-core.test.ts

nodes.name: getClaudeCredsCore
nodes.summary: Returns the full credential set (access token, refresh token, expiry) from the store after refreshing when needed, for consumers that require raw credentials.

nodes.name: first-login.test.ts

nodes.name: public-url.ts

nodes.summary: Compares two semver-style version strings numerically segment by segment.

nodes.name: releasesSince

nodes.name: notify.test.ts

nodes.name: useCurrentUserId
nodes.summary: Convenience hook returning just the current user's id, or null until loaded.

nodes.name: next-sprint.test.ts

nodes.name: nextSprintName
nodes.summary: Increments the last run of digits in an interval name preserving zero-padding ("Sprint 09" to "Sprint 10"), appending " 2" when the name has no digits.

nodes.name: computeNextSprintDefaults
nodes.summary: Computes the pre-filled name, start date, and end date for the follow-on sprint, starting the day after the completed sprint ends with the same duration.

nodes.name: subscribe.test.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Accepts both bare and { data }-wrapped VAPID key payloads — reading only the wrapped shape was a real bug that made every enable attempt fail.

nodes.name: enablePushNotifications

nodes.name: disablePushNotifications
nodes.summary: Unsubscribes the browser's existing push subscription and tells the server to delete it.

nodes.name: progress.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the key-result progress fraction covering increasing and lower-is-better metrics, clamping, and the degenerate start-equals-target cases.

nodes.summary: Single source of truth for the OKR key-result progress calculation, a clamped direction-agnostic fraction from start toward target, used by both API roll-ups and client views.
nodes.languageNotes: lowerIsBetter does not change the math for real ranges; it only disambiguates the start === target degenerate case.

nodes.name: krFraction
nodes.summary: Computes the clamped 0-1 fraction of a key result's progress from start to target, handling lower-is-better metrics and the start-equals-target edge case.

nodes.name: krProgressPercent
nodes.summary: Whole-percent (0-100) convenience wrapper around krFraction.

nodes.name: bulk.ts

nodes.summary: Runs an async op per id with Promise.allSettled, raising a partial-failure toast with counts via notifyError and returning how many succeeded and failed.

nodes.name: json-fetcher.ts

nodes.name: FetchError
nodes.summary: Error subclass carrying the HTTP status and parsed response body so error UIs can show server-provided messages.

nodes.name: jsonFetch
nodes.summary: Performs a fetch with JSON headers, tolerantly parses the response body, and throws a FetchError with the server's error message on non-2xx responses.

nodes.name: keys.ts
nodes.summary: Org-scoped React Query key helpers: derives the current org slug from the URL and builds ["org", slug, ...] query keys so an org switch automatically isolates and invalidates cached data.

nodes.name: useOrgSlug
nodes.summary: Reads the current org slug from the first URL path segment, returning null for reserved non-org routes like /onboarding, /admin, and /login.

nodes.name: useOrgQueryKey
nodes.summary: Hook that builds an org-scoped query key by prefixing the caller's parts with ["org", currentSlug].

nodes.name: orgQueryKey
nodes.summary: Non-hook variant that builds an org-scoped query key from an explicit slug, for use outside render (e.g. mutation invalidation).

nodes.name: use-org-mutation.ts
nodes.summary: useMutation wrapper used across the app that auto-invalidates the given org-scoped query subkeys on success and defaults onError to the notifyError toast.

nodes.name: useOrgMutation
nodes.summary: Generic mutation hook that invalidates each provided org-scoped subkey after success and shows an error toast by default unless the caller supplies its own onError.

nodes.name: permission-groups.ts
nodes.summary: Groups RBAC permission keys by their leading segment (e.g. ITEM_READ under "Item") and derives human labels, powering the role editor checklists and read-only permission breakdowns.
nodes.languageNotes: Extracted verbatim from roles-manager.tsx with a byte-identical output contract for existing importers.

nodes.name: groupOf
nodes.summary: Returns the title-cased leading segment of a permission key as its group name (ITEM_READ becomes "Item").

nodes.name: labelOf
nodes.summary: Builds a friendly sentence-cased label from a permission key's trailing segments (ITEM_READ becomes "Read").

nodes.name: health.test.ts

nodes.name: health.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately the only place the health comparison lives — every surface that colors a bar or pill imports these instead of re-deriving it.

nodes.name: healthOf
nodes.summary: Returns green, red, or neutral by comparing actual end (or now, while open) to the current projected end.

nodes.name: slipDays
nodes.summary: Whole-day schedule variance: (actualEnd or now) minus projectedEnd, positive meaning late, null when no projection exists.

nodes.name: error-report.ts

nodes.name: activity-label.test.ts

nodes.name: bulk-tags.test.ts

nodes.name: mapRoleCapped
nodes.summary: Maps IdP group memberships to an org role using the connection's group-role mapping, capping the result at the connection's maximum allowed role.

nodes.name: completeSsoLogin
nodes.summary: Finalizes an SSO callback: enforces the AAL floor, finds or creates the user and federated identity, upserts org membership with a capped role, consumes pending invitations, auto-joins the general chat channel, writes an audit log, and creates session records.

nodes.name: temp-password.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests that generated temporary passwords use the unambiguous alphabet, meet length requirements, and satisfy the password policy when hashed and verified.

nodes.name: temp-password.ts
nodes.summary: Generates cryptographically random temporary passwords from an alphabet that excludes visually ambiguous characters, used for password-based invitations.

nodes.name: generateTempPassword
nodes.summary: Builds a random temporary password of the requested length using crypto.randomInt over the unambiguous alphabet.

nodes.name: totp.ts
nodes.summary: Self-contained TOTP (RFC 6238) implementation for MFA: secret generation, base32 decoding, HOTP computation, timing-safe verification, otpauth URI building branded per deployment, and recovery-code generation, hashing, and consumption.
nodes.languageNotes: Implements HOTP/TOTP directly on Node's crypto primitives (HMAC-SHA1, timingSafeEqual) rather than pulling in an OTP library.

nodes.name: generateTotpSecret
nodes.summary: Generates a random base32-encoded TOTP secret from crypto random bytes.

nodes.name: base32Decode
nodes.summary: Decodes a base32 secret string into a byte buffer for HMAC keying.

nodes.name: hotp
nodes.summary: Computes an HOTP value for a key and counter using HMAC-SHA1 with dynamic truncation.

nodes.name: verifyTotp
nodes.summary: Verifies a user-supplied TOTP token against expected values across a time-step window using timing-safe comparison.

nodes.name: totpUri
nodes.summary: Builds an otpauth:// provisioning URI for authenticator apps, using the deployment brand as the issuer.

nodes.name: generateRecoveryCodes
nodes.summary: Generates a set of random, hyphen-formatted MFA recovery codes.

nodes.name: hashRecoveryCode
nodes.summary: Hashes a normalized recovery code with SHA-256 for storage.

nodes.name: consumeRecoveryCode
nodes.summary: Matches a supplied recovery code against stored hashes with timing-safe comparison and returns the remaining unused hashes.

nodes.name: seed-general.ts
nodes.summary: Ensures every organization has a default #general chat channel and auto-joins new members to it during org creation, invitation acceptance, and SSO login.

nodes.name: ensureGeneralChannel
nodes.summary: Finds or creates the org's #general chat channel, handling create races by re-querying.

nodes.name: autoJoinGeneral
nodes.summary: Upserts a membership in the org's #general channel for a user, used when members join an organization.

nodes.name: field-seal.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the field-seal wrapper: sealed-format detection, round-trip seal/open, plaintext passthrough, and self-healing re-seal behavior on key rotation.

nodes.name: field-seal.ts
nodes.summary: Field-level encryption wrapper over the vault: detects whether a stored value is sealed, seals and opens individual fields, and can transparently heal legacy or old-key values by re-sealing them via a callback.

nodes.name: isSealed
nodes.summary: Detects whether a stored string is in the sealed envelope format by validating its structure and key id.

nodes.name: sealField
nodes.summary: Seals a plaintext field value using the vault's active key.

nodes.name: openField
nodes.summary: Opens a stored field value, passing through plaintext values that were never sealed.

nodes.name: openFieldWithHeal
nodes.summary: Opens a stored value and, when it was plaintext or sealed under a non-active key, invokes a reseal callback so the row is healed to the current key.

nodes.name: vault.ts
nodes.summary: AES-256-GCM secret vault with a multi-key keyring loaded from environment variables: seals secrets under the active key id, opens values sealed under any known key (including a legacy v1 format), and rewraps old ciphertexts for key rotation.
nodes.languageNotes: Envelope format embeds a key id (kid) so rotation is possible without re-encrypting everything at once; rewrapSecret plus openFieldWithHeal implement lazy migration.

nodes.name: decodeKey
nodes.summary: Decodes and validates a base64 32-byte AES key from configuration, throwing a labeled error on bad input.

nodes.name: loadKeyring
nodes.summary: Parses the keyring environment (JSON map of kid to key plus active kid, or a single legacy key), validates key ids, and caches the resulting keyring.

nodes.name: keyForKid
nodes.summary: Looks up the AES key for a key id in the keyring, raising a descriptive error listing known kids when missing.

nodes.name: sealWith
nodes.summary: Encrypts plaintext with AES-256-GCM under a specific key and encodes the v2 envelope of kid, IV, auth tag, and ciphertext.

nodes.name: kidOf
nodes.summary: Parses a sealed string and returns the key id it was sealed under, distinguishing v1 legacy envelopes from v2.

nodes.name: activeKid
nodes.summary: Returns the currently active key id from the loaded keyring.

nodes.name: sealSecret
nodes.summary: Seals a plaintext secret under the keyring's active key.

nodes.name: openSecret
nodes.summary: Decrypts a sealed secret, supporting both the v2 kid-tagged envelope and the legacy v1 format.

nodes.name: rewrapSecret
nodes.summary: Re-encrypts a secret sealed under an old key with the active key, returning it unchanged if already current.

nodes.name: freeze.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the cutover freeze helpers: mutating-method detection, extracting org references from API and dashboard paths, and freeze lookups by slug or id.

nodes.name: freeze.ts
nodes.summary: Cutover freeze machinery that marks organizations read-only during migration: parses org references out of request paths, checks the FrozenOrg table, and exposes freeze/unfreeze operations.

nodes.name: isMutatingMethod
nodes.summary: Returns whether an HTTP method is a mutating verb that should be blocked for frozen orgs.

nodes.name: orgRefFromPath
nodes.summary: Extracts an org id or slug reference from an API v1 path or a dashboard path, ignoring known non-org top-level segments.

nodes.name: isOrgFrozen
nodes.summary: Checks the FrozenOrg table by slug to see if an organization is frozen.

nodes.name: isPathOrgFrozen
nodes.summary: Resolves the org referenced by a request path and reports whether that org is currently frozen.

nodes.name: freezeOrg
nodes.summary: Upserts a FrozenOrg row to place an organization into read-only cutover mode with optional metadata.

nodes.name: unfreezeOrg
nodes.summary: Removes an organization's freeze record, restoring write access.

nodes.name: email-sender.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the transactional email sender across environment and org-config combinations, stubbing fetch to verify provider payloads, sender resolution, and error handling.

nodes.name: email-sender.ts
nodes.summary: Transactional email sender that resolves per-org email configuration (falling back to environment defaults) and posts messages to the configured HTTP email provider API, reporting whether sending is configured at all.

nodes.name: isTransactionalEmailConfigured
nodes.summary: Reports whether a usable transactional email configuration exists for the org or environment.

nodes.name: sendAppEmail
nodes.summary: Sends a transactional email by loading the org email config and POSTing subject, text, and HTML bodies to the provider API, surfacing provider errors from the response.

nodes.name: invitation-email.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests invitation, password-invite, and password-reset email composition and dispatch, verifying transactional-vs-Gmail routing and message content.

nodes.name: invitation-email.ts
nodes.summary: Composes branded invitation, temporary-password invite, and password-reset emails and dispatches them through the org's transactional sender, falling back to sending via the inviter's Gmail account.

nodes.name: sendViaGmail
nodes.summary: Builds a MIME multipart message and sends it through the inviter's Gmail account via the Google API client.

nodes.name: lookupInviterEmail
nodes.summary: Loads the inviting user's email address from the database for use as the Gmail sender.

nodes.name: dispatchInviteEmail
nodes.summary: Routes an invite email through the transactional sender when configured, otherwise falls back to the inviter's Gmail account.

nodes.name: sendInvitationEmail
nodes.summary: Composes and dispatches a branded Google-sign-in invitation email with an accept link.

nodes.name: sendPasswordInviteEmail
nodes.summary: Composes and dispatches a password-based invitation email, including a temporary password and MFA note when applicable.

nodes.name: sendPasswordResetEmail
nodes.summary: Composes a single-use password-reset email with an expiring link and sends it through the transactional sender.

nodes.name: mcp-secrets.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests sealing and unsealing of MCP server env/header secret maps, including round-trips and handling of malformed stored values.

nodes.name: mcp-secrets.ts
nodes.summary: Seals and unseals MCP server secret maps (env vars and HTTP headers) as encrypted JSON blobs using the field-seal layer, with typed accessors per server record.

nodes.name: sealMcpJson
nodes.summary: Serializes a non-empty secret map to JSON and seals it for storage.

nodes.name: openMcpJson
nodes.summary: Opens a sealed JSON blob and validates that it is a flat string-to-string map before returning it.

nodes.name: unsealMcpJson
nodes.summary: Public wrapper that unseals a stored MCP secret map.

nodes.name: getMcpEnv
nodes.summary: Returns the decrypted environment-variable map for an MCP server record.

nodes.name: getMcpHeaders
nodes.summary: Returns the decrypted HTTP header map for an MCP server record.

nodes.name: org-email-config.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests org email configuration resolution using sealed API-key fixtures, covering DB-backed settings, environment fallback, and API-key unsealing.

nodes.name: org-email-config.ts
nodes.summary: Resolves an organization's transactional email configuration from the OrgEmailSettings table, unsealing the vault-sealed provider API key and falling back to environment defaults.

nodes.name: hasSealedApiKey
nodes.summary: Checks whether a stored settings value contains a sealed API-key record.

nodes.name: unsealApiKey
nodes.summary: Opens the vault-sealed provider API key from a settings record, returning null on failure.

nodes.name: getOrgEmailConfig
nodes.summary: Loads the org's email settings row, merges it with environment fallbacks, and returns a usable sender configuration with the unsealed API key.

nodes.name: webhook-dispatch.ts
nodes.summary: Fans out an org event to all matching active webhooks: signs the JSON payload with each hook's HMAC secret (healing sealed secrets on read), records a delivery row, POSTs with a timeout, and stores the delivery outcome.

nodes.name: dispatchWebhook
nodes.summary: Delivers an event payload to every subscribed org webhook with an HMAC-SHA256 signature, timeout-bounded fetch, and per-delivery success/failure records.

nodes.name: webhook-seal.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests that webhook signing secrets round-trip through the field-seal layer and that HMAC signatures computed from unsealed secrets match expectations.

nodes.name: bucket.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the in-memory token-bucket rate limiter, covering allowance under the limit, blocking over it, and window refill behavior.

nodes.name: bucket.ts
nodes.summary: In-memory token-bucket rate limiter with periodic pruning of stale buckets and a helper that derives rate-limit keys from route id plus user id or forwarded client IP.
nodes.languageNotes: Per-process Map-based buckets; suitable for a single Node instance rather than distributed rate limiting.

nodes.name: rateLimit
nodes.summary: Applies token-bucket accounting for a key, returning whether the request is allowed along with remaining tokens and retry-after timing.

nodes.name: getRateLimitKey
nodes.summary: Builds a rate-limit key from the route id and the user id, falling back to the x-forwarded-for or x-real-ip client address.

nodes.name: headers.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the standard security response headers (CSP-adjacent hardening such as frame, content-type, and referrer policies) and a helper that applies them to a Headers object.

nodes.name: applySecurityHeaders
nodes.summary: Copies every configured security header onto the given response Headers object.

nodes.name: cookie.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests theme and skin cookie validators, accepting known modes and skin ids and rejecting invalid values.

nodes.name: cookie.ts
nodes.summary: Declares the theme-mode and skin cookie names and validators that check values against the allowed theme modes and registered skin presets.

nodes.name: isValidThemeMode
nodes.summary: Type guard validating that a cookie value is a supported theme mode.

nodes.name: isValidSkinId
nodes.summary: Validates a skin id against the registered skin presets.

nodes.name: proxy.ts
nodes.summary: Next.js middleware entry point that guards every request: applies security headers, enforces same-origin CSRF checks on mutating calls (with exemptions for API-token and webhook paths), blocks writes to frozen orgs during cutover, validates the session cookie against the database, and redirects unauthenticated users to login.
nodes.languageNotes: Exports a Next.js `config` matcher alongside the proxy handler; session lookup hits Prisma directly, so this middleware runs in the Node runtime rather than the Edge runtime.

nodes.name: isSameOrigin
nodes.summary: Compares Origin/Referer headers against the request host to enforce same-origin CSRF protection.

nodes.name: proxy
nodes.summary: Main request gate: rejects cross-origin mutations, returns 423-style errors for frozen orgs, passes public paths through, validates the session cookie, allows bearer-token API access, and otherwise redirects to the login page — always with security headers applied.

nodes.name: m365-connector-accept.ts
nodes.summary: Standalone acceptance script that end-to-end verifies the Microsoft 365 connector: sealed install of Entra credentials, config/secret splitting, cached Graph token exchange against a mocked fetch, tool execution, and gov-tenant egress projection that withholds content fields.

nodes.name: runtime-config-accept.ts
nodes.summary: Acceptance script for per-org runtime config: verifies gov guardrails are applied when a tenant flips to gov, guardrail violation detection, and connector tool-def gating by enabledConnectors and breadth settings.

nodes.name: agent-policy-acceptance.test.ts
nodes.summary: Docker acceptance test for the AgentPolicy 3-axis gate, run against real containerized Postgres with only the model stub and tool executor mocked: proves domain/tool refusals, result-limit clamping in the agent loop, and RBAC on the policy API.

nodes.name: handle-flag-off-acceptance.ts
nodes.summary: Acceptance script proving the EGRESS_HANDLES_ENABLED=off legacy path: withheld fields are dropped without minting opaque handles and handle-shaped strings resolve to nothing.

nodes.name: handle-resolver-acceptance.ts
nodes.summary: Acceptance script for the opaque-handle egress resolver: mints handles for withheld CUI fields, verifies sealed storage, org-scoped deep resolution, tamper/expiry behavior, and classification-ceiling projection.

nodes.name: native-connectors-acceptance.ts
nodes.summary: Acceptance script for the native token-auth connectors (Jira, Slack): sealed install of org credentials with secrets stripped from persisted config, tool execution against mocked HTTP, and gov versus commercial egress projection of results.

nodes.name: write-path-taint-acceptance.ts
nodes.summary: Acceptance script for write-path taint enforcement: resolving handles during a write raises the effective classification ceiling, blocking writes into lower-classified targets and logging the egress decision.

nodes.name: exposability-snapshot.mjs
nodes.summary: CLI that snapshots the complete effective egress exposability map into canonical JSON, reviewer-facing Markdown, and a stable sha256 hash — the artifacts a security reviewer signs off before a GOV tenant cutover flip.

nodes.name: exposability.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the exposability snapshot and sign-off library: canonicalization stability, hash sensitivity to field changes, and the fail-closed GOV sign-off gate with an injected sign-off loader.

nodes.name: exposability.ts
nodes.summary: Assembles the complete effective exposability map from the live egress code (never a re-hardcoded copy), produces a canonical serialization and sha256 hash, and gates GOV cutover flips fail-closed on a leak-tested human sign-off bound to the current hash.

nodes.name: mockGraphFetch
nodes.summary: Builds a fetch stub that records requested URLs and returns a canned token or Graph response body so the acceptance flow runs fully offline.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Drives the full M365 acceptance flow: creates an org and user, installs sealed Entra credentials, exercises cached Graph token exchange and tool execution against mocked fetch, and asserts gov egress withholds content fields.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates orgs in the database, flips one to gov to verify guardrails are applied transactionally, checks violation detection, and asserts connector tool defs are gated by enabledConnectors and breadth.

nodes.name: driveOneTool
nodes.summary: Stubs one model turn that requests a single tool call, runs the real agent loop against the container DB, and returns the message transcript so assertions can inspect tool_result blocks.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: With the handles flag off, projects a synthetic tool result and checks no handle tokens are minted, no EgressHandle rows are written, and deep resolution passes values through untouched.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Mints handles by projecting withheld fields, verifies sealed storage and org-scoped resolution, exercises expiry/tamper and embedded-handle cases, and checks ceiling-based projection withholds for a commercial credential.

nodes.name: install
nodes.summary: Installs a provider integration for an org: splits secret keys out of config, seals them as an org credential, and creates the Integration row with the sanitized config.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the Jira and Slack native-connector acceptance: sealed installs, not-connected errors, tool execution against mocked HTTP, and gov versus commercial model-view projection of the results.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Seeds classified projects and work item types, mints a handle from a CUI field, then proves a write whose resolved inputs exceed the target's ceiling is blocked, logged, and never persisted.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses the CLI flags (notably --out) into an options object, failing fast on unknown arguments.

nodes.name: renderMarkdown
nodes.summary: Renders the exposability map as reviewer-facing Markdown: per entity type the exposed structural fields, contributing tools, an explicit default-deny note, fully-withheld tool families, and the map hash.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Assembles the live exposability map, then writes the canonical JSON, Markdown rendering, and bare hash files into the requested output directory.

nodes.name: getExposabilityMap
nodes.summary: Assembles the complete effective exposability map from the live projection maps and connector registry contributions — the same merged maps the egress gate enforces, so the snapshot can never drift from enforcement.

nodes.name: canonicalize
nodes.summary: Produces a canonical, stable serialization of the exposability map with sorted keys and sorted arrays so identical maps always serialize identically.

nodes.name: exposabilityHash
nodes.summary: Computes the sha256 hash over the canonical map serialization; a sign-off is bound to this hash.

nodes.name: isSignoff
nodes.summary: Runtime type guard validating that a parsed sign-off record has the required shape (slug, mapHash, leakTestPassed, reviewer fields).

nodes.name: requireExposabilitySignoff
nodes.summary: The GOV-flip gate: for a gov tenant, requires a sign-off record whose mapHash matches the current exposability hash and whose leak test passed; missing, stale, or leak-failed sign-offs fail closed, while commercial tenants pass unconditionally.

nodes.name: signoffPath
nodes.summary: Resolves the canonical filesystem path for an org's sign-off record under compliance/exposability/signoff/.

nodes.name: loadSignoffFromDisk
nodes.summary: Default sign-off loader that reads and parses the org's sign-off JSON from disk, returning undefined when absent.

nodes.name: proxy-control.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the cutover proxy control library: pure Caddy route/config builders, desired-state decoding, and ProxyControl freeze/unfreeze/set-upstream mutations against an in-memory mock Caddy admin API.

nodes.name: proxy-control.ts
nodes.summary: Caddy admin-API client plus pure config builders for per-tenant cutover freeze/flip/rollback: derives the full route list (freeze, upstream, fallback) from a desired per-org state object and applies idempotent mutations via atomic POST /load.

nodes.name: snapshot.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the PITR snapshot helpers: restore-point label validation, restore-point SQL, mandatory-target pgBackRest restore command construction, and snapshot record build/parse round-trips.

nodes.name: snapshot.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, side-effect-free helpers for pre-flip PITR snapshot capture and restore: builds pg_create_restore_point SQL, precise pgBackRest restore commands (a target is mandatory), and validated snapshot records; nothing here ever executes a restore.

nodes.name: orchestrate.mjs
nodes.summary: The per-tenant cutover orchestrator CLI: freezes the org at the proxy, captures a PITR snapshot (optionally drill-validating it), runs sync/soak cycles, enforces the GOV exposability sign-off gate, flips the upstream to v2, and emits precise rollback commands on failure.

nodes.name: snapshot-capture.mjs
nodes.summary: CLI that stamps a named PITR restore point (recording LSN, server time, and timeline), optionally triggers an incremental pgBackRest backup, and merges the snapshot evidence record into the cutover state file.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route reporting whether the current user has a Google connection, via a presence check on the sealed connector credential store; the sealed secret is never opened.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route for a single org integration: GET details, PUT updates that re-split secret keys out of config into the sealed org-credential store, and DELETE with credential cleanup — all INTEGRATION_MANAGE-gated and audited.

nodes.name: route.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the org integrations collection route with mocked auth and Prisma, covering RBAC enforcement and provider validation on POST.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route listing an org's integrations and creating new ones from registry providers, splitting secret config keys into the sealed org-credential store so plaintext secrets never persist; INTEGRATION_MANAGE-gated and audited.

nodes.name: mockCaddy
nodes.summary: In-memory stub of the Caddy admin API that serves the current config and accepts full /load replacements so ProxyControl mutations are testable without a live proxy.

nodes.name: frozenBody
nodes.summary: Builds the JSON org_frozen 405 response body served to writes against a frozen org.

nodes.name: orgPathPatterns
nodes.summary: Returns the Caddy path matchers for an org slug (the /<slug> and /<slug>/* dashboard route shapes).

nodes.name: buildFreezeRoute
nodes.summary: Builds the per-org freeze route: mutating methods on the org's paths get a 405 static response with an Allow header, while reads fall through to the upstream route.

nodes.name: buildUpstreamRoute
nodes.summary: Builds the per-org reverse_proxy route pointing the org's path prefix at a non-default (v2) upstream dial.

nodes.name: buildFallbackRoute
nodes.summary: Builds the catch-all reverse_proxy route that sends all unmatched traffic to the default (v1) upstream.

nodes.name: buildRoutes
nodes.summary: Derives the ordered Caddy route list (freeze routes, then non-default upstream routes, then the fallback) from the desired per-org state object.

nodes.name: buildCaddyConfig
nodes.summary: Builds the complete Caddy config (admin listener, HTTP server, derived routes) from desired state and upstream dials — the single artifact POSTed atomically via /load.

nodes.name: decodeState
nodes.summary: Decodes the per-org { upstream, frozen } state back out of a live Caddy config's route list, the inverse of buildRoutes.

nodes.name: applyFreeze
nodes.summary: Pure state transition marking an org frozen in the desired-state object.

nodes.name: applyUnfreeze
nodes.summary: Pure state transition clearing an org's frozen flag in the desired-state object.

nodes.name: applySetUpstream
nodes.summary: Pure state transition setting an org's upstream dial (v1/v2) in the desired-state object.

nodes.name: ProxyControl
nodes.summary: Client for the cutover Caddy admin API: fetches the live config with retry, decodes per-org state, applies one idempotent freeze/unfreeze/set-upstream change, and atomically re-POSTs the fully re-derived config via /load.

nodes.name: assertValidLabel
nodes.summary: Validates a restore-point label against a conservative shell- and SQL-safe character set, throwing on anything else.

nodes.name: buildCreateRestorePointSql
nodes.summary: Builds the SELECT pg_create_restore_point SQL for a validated, quote-escaped label that stamps a named PITR target into the WAL.

nodes.name: buildRestoreArgv
nodes.summary: Builds the pgBackRest restore argv for a captured point, requiring a named or time target and throwing rather than ever emitting a targetless (end-of-WAL) restore.

nodes.name: buildRestoreCommand
nodes.summary: Renders the restore argv as a single shell-quoted command string for an operator to run by hand.

nodes.name: buildSnapshotRecord
nodes.summary: Assembles the validated snapshot record (label, LSN, restore-point time, stanza, timeline, capturedAt, optional backup label) persisted into the cutover state file.

nodes.name: parseSnapshotRecord
nodes.summary: Validates and parses a snapshot record read back from the cutover state, rejecting malformed or incomplete records.

nodes.name: restoreCommandsForRecord
nodes.summary: Produces the precise named-target and time-target pgBackRest restore commands for a captured snapshot record — the rollback instructions the orchestrator emits but never executes.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses the orchestrator's CLI flags (org, slug, database URLs, proxy admin, upstream dials, tenant class, snapshot options) into an options object.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Spawns a child command, streams its output, and returns the captured stdout, failing the step on a non-zero exit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs the full cutover sequence for one tenant: proxy freeze, snapshot capture (and optional restore drill), sync/soak cycles until quiesced, the GOV exposability sign-off gate, the upstream flip to v2, and post-flip verification, invoking rollback on any failure.

nodes.name: rollback
nodes.summary: Reverts a failed flip: repoints the org's upstream back to v1, unfreezes it at the proxy, and emits (never executes) the precise pgBackRest restore commands for the captured snapshot.

nodes.name: parseSoakUpserts
nodes.summary: Extracts the upsert count from a soak-cycle child process's stdout so the loop can detect quiescence.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses the capture CLI's flags (--db, --label, --stamp, --state, stanza and pgBackRest options) into an options object.

nodes.name: run
nodes.summary: Runs a child command and returns its trimmed stdout, failing the script on a non-zero exit.

nodes.name: loadState
nodes.summary: Loads and parses the cutover state JSON file, returning an empty object when the file does not yet exist.

nodes.name: triggerIncrBackupAndLabel
nodes.summary: Triggers an incremental pgBackRest backup through the configured exec prefix and extracts the resulting backup label from pgbackrest info.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Stamps the named restore point via psql, captures LSN, server time, and timeline, optionally triggers the incremental backup, and merges the snapshot record into the state file without clobbering soak watermarks.

nodes.name: descriptors.test.ts

nodes.name: conversation-title.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests for AI conversation title generation, covering title cleaning rules (quotes, prefixes, length caps) and fallback behavior when the model output is unusable.

nodes.name: conversation-title.ts
nodes.summary: Generates a short title for an assistant conversation by running a model turn through the egress chokepoint over the first user/assistant messages, then sanitizing the raw output with cleanTitle and falling back to DEFAULT_CONVERSATION_TITLE.

nodes.name: registerConnector
nodes.summary: Registers a ConnectorDescriptor, validating global tool-name uniqueness across descriptors and consistency between a descriptor's tool defs and its egress map keys before adding it.

nodes.name: getConnectorDescriptors
nodes.summary: Returns the currently registered connector descriptors as a read-only snapshot.

nodes.name: allConnectorProviders
nodes.summary: Lists the provider ids of every registered connector descriptor.

nodes.name: commercialOnlyProviders
nodes.summary: Lists the provider ids of connectors whose availability is commercial-only, i.e. the set that must be invisible to government tenants.

nodes.name: connectorToolDefs
nodes.summary: Flattens tool definitions from all descriptors visible to a tenant class, further narrowed by the org's runtime-config enablement filter.

nodes.name: connectorToolNames
nodes.summary: Returns the set of connector tool names available to a tenant class under the current runtime-config enablement, derived from the tool-name ownership map.

nodes.name: executeConnectorTool
nodes.summary: Dispatches a connector tool call to its owning descriptor's executor, hard-refusing (with an audit-logged egress decision and hashed input) when the tenant class is not allowed or the provider is disabled by runtime config.

nodes.name: connectorEgressMaps
nodes.summary: Merges every descriptor's TOOL_ENTITY, EXPOSABLE_FIELDS, and HANDLEABLE_FIELDS contributions into the combined egress maps, asserting consistency when two descriptors define the same key.

nodes.name: resetConnectors
nodes.summary: Clears the registry's descriptor list and tool-name ownership map; a test-only escape hatch for isolating registration state between test cases.

nodes.name: cleanTitle
nodes.summary: Sanitizes raw model output into a usable conversation title: takes the first non-empty line, strips 'Title:' prefixes, surrounding quotes, and trailing punctuation, and truncates to the maximum length.

nodes.name: generateConversationTitle
nodes.summary: Generates a conversation title by running a single model turn through the egress-controlled runModelTurn over truncated first user/assistant messages, then cleaning the result and falling back to the default title on failure.

nodes.name: gate.test.ts

nodes.name: observe-only.test.ts

nodes.name: projection.test.ts

nodes.name: audit.ts
nodes.summary: Persists egress decisions (content hash, exposure verdict, withheld counts — never CUI itself) to the EgressDecisionRow table and emits observability metrics, swallowing storage failures with a warning.

nodes.name: augment.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests augmentWithHandles: withheld handleable fields on projected tool results are replaced with opaque handles, across single entities, arrays, and keyed collections.

nodes.name: gate.ts
nodes.summary: The core egress gate: projectForModel decides whether a value may cross to the model by comparing its classification against the org ceiling and scanning for CUI markings, returning an exposure decision with a sha256 content hash for the audit trail.

nodes.name: handles.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the opaque-handle lifecycle: token format recognition, minting sealed handles, per-conversation resolution scoping, and deep resolution of handles nested in tool-call arguments with ceiling maximization.

nodes.name: handles.ts
nodes.summary: Opaque-handle subsystem for CUI-by-reference: mints random tokens whose values are vault-sealed into the EgressHandle table, resolves them scoped to a conversation, and deep-walks tool inputs to substitute handles back with their plaintext while tracking the maximum classification ceiling touched.
nodes.languageNotes: Handles are crypto.randomBytes tokens with a recognizable prefix; plaintext never leaves the database unsealed except through conversation-scoped resolution.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: The single egress chokepoint and public barrel for the egress layer: runModelTurn gates system/user/tool values through projectForModel, runs the CUI classifier, logs every decision, resolves the org/user model credential, and calls the model provider inside an OpenTelemetry span.

nodes.name: projection.ts
nodes.summary: Field-level exposure policy for tool results: per-entity EXPOSABLE_FIELDS and HANDLEABLE_FIELDS allowlists plus TOOL_ENTITY mapping (merged with connector-declared maps), with projection helpers that strip non-exposable fields and augmentation that swaps withheld handleable fields for opaque handles.

nodes.name: logEgressDecision
nodes.summary: Records an egress decision to metrics and persists it to the EgressDecisionRow table (content hash and counts only, never CUI), logging a warning instead of throwing if the write fails.

nodes.name: sha256Hex
nodes.summary: Computes the sha256 hex digest of a serialized value, used as tamper-evident content hashing for egress audit records.

nodes.name: projectForModel
nodes.summary: The gate verdict function: decides whether a value is exposed to the model or withheld by ranking its classification against the ceiling and detecting CUI markings, returning the decision plus content hash.

nodes.name: isHandle
nodes.summary: Checks whether a string matches the opaque-handle token format (known prefix plus valid token body).

nodes.name: mintHandle
nodes.summary: Mints a new opaque handle for a withheld value: seals the plaintext with the vault, generates a random token, and stores the sealed record with its classification ceiling scoped to the conversation.

nodes.name: resolveHandle
nodes.summary: Resolves an opaque handle token back to its plaintext value by looking up the sealed record scoped to the conversation and opening it with the vault; returns null for unknown or foreign-conversation tokens.

nodes.name: resolveHandlesDeep
nodes.summary: Recursively walks an arbitrary tool-input structure, replacing every embedded handle token with its resolved plaintext and accumulating the maximum classification ceiling of all touched handles.

nodes.name: toModelTools
nodes.summary: Maps internal tool definitions to the model-facing ModelTool shape expected by the provider layer.

nodes.name: runModelTurn
nodes.summary: The single model-call chokepoint: computes the effective classification ceiling, gates system and message values through projectForModel with per-value audit logging, runs the CUI classifier as an observer, resolves the org/user model credential, and invokes callModel within a traced span with error metrics.

nodes.name: entityTypeForTool
nodes.summary: Looks up the entity type a tool's results belong to via the merged TOOL_ENTITY map (static entries plus connector-declared entries).

nodes.name: projectOne
nodes.summary: Projects a single entity object down to its exposable-field allowlist, dropping every field not explicitly permitted for model visibility.

nodes.name: projectStructural
nodes.summary: Applies the exposable-field projection to a value or array of values for a given entity type, preserving structure.

nodes.name: projectResult
nodes.summary: Projects a full tool result for an entity type, handling plain objects, arrays, and container objects whose keys hold entity arrays, so only allowlisted fields reach the model.

nodes.name: augmentOneEntity
nodes.summary: For one projected entity, mints opaque handles for handleable fields that were withheld from the model view and attaches the handle tokens in place of the plaintext.

nodes.name: augmentWithHandles
nodes.summary: Walks a projected model view alongside its source output (entities, arrays, or keyed collections) and augments each entity with opaque handles for withheld handleable fields, scoped to the conversation and ceiling.

nodes.name: provider.ts
nodes.summary: Stateless model-calling provider behind the egress chokepoint: callModel routes to the Anthropic SDK (API key or Claude subscription OAuth) or to a raw OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions endpoint over fetch, with streaming support, message/tool shape conversion, and finish-reason normalization.
nodes.languageNotes: The OpenAI path parses server-sent-event stream chunks by hand and accumulates tool-call deltas in a Map instead of using an SDK.

nodes.name: types.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free type module for the egress layer: TenantClass, ModelCredential variants (apiKey/oauth/openai), ValueKind, EgressMode, EgressContext, and the CUI-free EgressDecision audit record, plus the isWithheld guard.

nodes.name: isWithheld
