nodes.summary: Executor for the Nango connector tools — the commercial-only unified-API path that routes agent tool calls (list/get connections, proxy requests) through the in-boundary Nango broker, org-scoped. Hard-refuses gov tenants at the top of every entry as the last defense-in-depth layer (D5 gov-block layer 3).
nodes.languageNotes: Implements a triple-layered governance block: even though gov tenants never see these tools upstream, the executor independently re-checks tenantClass before any broker call.

nodes.name: slack.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the Slack tool executors, mocking fetch and the credential layer to verify channel listing, message search, safe posting, and egress projection of Slack API responses.

nodes.name: slack.ts
nodes.summary: Slack tool executors for the AI assistant — read-focused (list channels, search messages) plus one safe write (post message). Resolves the org-shared sealed bot token via getOrgCredential and calls the Slack Web API with graceful error returns so the model can recover from a missing connection.
nodes.languageNotes: Slack returns HTTP 200 with {ok:false,error} on failures, so the executor inspects the body rather than the status code; all tools funnel through a safeRun wrapper that converts throws into {error} results.

nodes.name: model-credential-provider.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the model-credential provider registry, covering the fail-safe null result when no provider is registered and delegation once a provider is installed.

nodes.name: model-credential-provider.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-inversion seam (ADR 0003) that lets core's feedback-intake LLM judges obtain a model credential without importing the Foreman plugin: Foreman registers a provider at composition time, and resolveModelCredential fails safe to null when nothing is registered.
nodes.languageNotes: Module-level singleton registry used to break a core-to-plugin coupling so the Foreman plugin can be extracted to its own repo.

nodes.name: domains.test.ts
nodes.summary: Arch/contract test asserting that every registered tool name — native cosmosTools plus every connector tool — has an explicit entry in the TOOL_DOMAIN map, so new tools surface as a deliberate policy edit.

nodes.name: domains.ts
nodes.summary: Flat, exhaustive tool-to-coarse-data-domain map powering the AgentPolicy DOMAIN axis: deniedDomains on an org policy blocks every tool whose domain is listed. Exports KNOWN_DOMAINS, the TOOL_DOMAIN record, and the domainForTool lookup with a DEFAULT_DOMAIN fallback for unknown tools.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately kept as one flat explicit record (not derived) so reviewers can audit each domain's blast radius at a glance; a contract test enforces exhaustiveness.

nodes.name: enforce.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for checkAgentPolicy covering all three policy axes — tool allow/deny lists, domain denial, and argument bounds — including precedence rules like denylist beating allowlist and clamping behavior.

nodes.name: enforce.ts
nodes.summary: Pure 3-axis AgentPolicy decision function (checkAgentPolicy) called by the agent loop before every tool execution: evaluates deniedTools/allowedTools, then tool domain denial, then argument constraints (projectId allowlist, numeric bounds), with first-deny-wins semantics.
nodes.languageNotes: Intentionally pure — never touches the DB, model, or CUI — so the whole policy gate is exhaustively unit-testable.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Per-org AgentPolicy loader that reads the AgentPolicy row from Prisma and normalizes it into the shape consumed by checkAgentPolicy, with a load-bearing permissive default when no row exists so pre-policy orgs behave unchanged.

nodes.name: tools.ts
nodes.summary: Central AI tool registry: defines the ToolDefinition type, aggregates all native tool catalogs (work items, OKRs, finance, CRM, boards, PM registers, etc.) plus connector tool defs into the cosmosTools array, re-exports every catalog, and formats tool schemas for the system prompt.
nodes.languageNotes: Acts as the single composition point for the agent's tool surface — 20 catalog imports merged into one exported array consumed by the agent loop and chat bots.

nodes.name: accounting.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring the accounting query tools (e.g. trial balance and ledger reads) exposed to the AI assistant as Anthropic tool schemas.

nodes.name: boards.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring board-related tools for the AI assistant, letting it query kanban board state.

nodes.name: comments.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring comment tools for the AI assistant, enabling reading and posting comments on work items and other subjects.

nodes.name: compliance.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring compliance-control query tools scoped to security frameworks (NIST 800-171, CMMC L2, FedRAMP, etc.) and implementation statuses.

nodes.name: crm.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog adding CRM write tools (create/update contacts) and partner/product list reads, mirroring the org CRM HTTP routes so assistant writes follow the same paths as human ones.

nodes.name: documents.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring document tools for the AI assistant, letting it list and read org documents.

nodes.name: feedback.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring feedback-portal tools for the AI assistant, covering feedback item queries and status interactions.

nodes.name: finance.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring finance tools (e.g. query_finance, revenue logging) exposed to the AI assistant.

nodes.name: github.ts
nodes.summary: GitHub tool catalog for the AI assistant — read-only issue and pull-request tools requiring an org-level sealed fine-grained PAT; executors live in the matching executors/github.ts and are wired via the connector registry.

nodes.name: goals-kpis.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring goal and KPI tools for the AI assistant, covering goal/KPI queries and progress updates.

nodes.name: google.ts
nodes.summary: Google Workspace tool catalog for the AI chat (Gmail, Calendar, Drive reads and related actions); every tool requires the calling user's Google refresh token, with executors in executors/google.ts dispatched from the tool executor.

nodes.name: jira.ts
nodes.summary: Jira Cloud tool catalog for the AI assistant — read-focused issue/search tools plus one safe write, backed by an org-shared sealed Atlassian API token credential.

nodes.name: meetings.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring meeting tools for the AI assistant, covering meeting queries and note/action-item access.

nodes.name: microsoft365.ts
nodes.summary: Microsoft 365 (Graph API) tool catalog for the AI assistant — read-only tools backed by an org-shared Entra app registration sealed into the org vault credential, using OAuth2 client-credentials auth.

nodes.name: milestones.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring milestone tools for the AI assistant, covering milestone queries and updates.

nodes.name: nango.ts
nodes.summary: Nango tool catalog — the commercial-only unified-API breadth path letting the assistant act against ~180 SaaS providers through the self-hosted Nango broker; credentials stay inside Nango and are org-scoped, with executors in executors/nango.ts.

nodes.name: notes.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring note tools for the AI assistant, covering note creation and retrieval.

nodes.name: okrs.ts
nodes.summary: Tool catalog declaring OKR tools for the AI assistant, covering objective/key-result queries, creation, and progress updates.

nodes.name: pm-register.ts
nodes.summary: PM Dashboard register tool catalog letting the assistant read and update the govcon PM registers — risks, blockers, deliverables, change requests — and comment on drill-in subjects; writes mirror the project risk HTTP routes so auto-coding and activity logging stay identical for humans and the assistant.

nodes.name: executeNangoTool
nodes.summary: Dispatches the three Nango tools (list connections, get connection, proxy request) against the org-scoped Nango client after hard-refusing gov tenants and unknown tool names.

nodes.name: resolveSlackAccess
nodes.summary: Resolves the org's sealed Slack bot token via getOrgCredential and the optional defaultChannel from the plaintext Integration config row.

nodes.name: slackCall
nodes.summary: Low-level Slack Web API caller that sends authenticated GET/POST requests and normalizes Slack's 200-with-ok:false error convention into thrown errors.

nodes.name: slackListChannels
nodes.summary: Lists the workspace's public/private channels via conversations.list with a clamped limit, projecting each channel to a minimal safe shape.

nodes.name: slackSearchMessages
nodes.summary: Searches Slack messages via search.messages with query trimming, clamped result count, and projection of matches to a compact result shape.

nodes.name: slackPostMessage
nodes.summary: The single safe Slack write: posts a message via chat.postMessage to an explicit channel or the integration's configured default channel, validating non-empty text.

nodes.name: executeSlackTool
nodes.summary: Dispatch entry point mapping the three Slack tool names to their executor functions, returning an error result for unknown names.

nodes.name: registerModelCredentialProvider
nodes.summary: Registers the singleton model-credential resolver, called by the Foreman plugin's server hooks at composition time.

nodes.name: resolveModelCredential
nodes.summary: Resolves a per-org model credential through the registered provider, returning null (never throwing) when no provider is registered or the resolver fails, so intake judges degrade gracefully.

nodes.name: domainForTool
nodes.summary: Looks up a tool's coarse data-domain in TOOL_DOMAIN, falling back to DEFAULT_DOMAIN for unknown tool names.

nodes.name: checkAgentPolicy
nodes.summary: Pure decision function for the AgentPolicy gate: evaluates the tool allow/deny axis, the domain-denial axis, and the args axis (projectId allowlist and numeric clamps) in order, with first deny winning.

nodes.name: getAgentPolicy
nodes.summary: Loads the org's AgentPolicy row via Prisma and normalizes it, returning the permissive default when no row exists.

nodes.name: normalizeAgentPolicy
nodes.summary: Converts a raw AgentPolicy DB row (or null) into the clean AgentPolicy shape consumed by checkAgentPolicy, applying the permissive defaults for missing fields.

nodes.name: formatToolsForSystemPrompt
nodes.summary: Renders an array of tool definitions into a plain-text block (name, description, JSON schema) for embedding in the agent's system prompt.

nodes.name: projects.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the projectTools catalog of AI assistant tool definitions for project operations (list_projects with fuzzy name/key resolution, create_project, update_project), each with a JSON input schema consumed by the chat agent's tool registry.

nodes.name: rag.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the ragTools catalog containing the semantic_search tool definition, letting the AI assistant search notes, work items, contracts, and meetings by similarity score.

nodes.name: slack.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the slackTools catalog for the AI assistant: read-focused Slack tools (list channels, search messages) plus one safe write (post message), using the org-level Slack bot token and routing results through the egress chokepoint so gov tenants only see structural fields.
nodes.languageNotes: Extensive doc comments encode the security model: org-shared bot token from the vault, executors dispatched via the connector registry, and structural-only projection for gov tenants.

nodes.name: time.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the timeTools catalog of AI assistant tool definitions for time-tracking operations, each entry pairing a tool name and description with a JSON input schema.

nodes.name: utility.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the utilityTools catalog containing the fetch_url tool, which fetches a public http(s) URL as stripped text while refusing localhost/private IPs and not following redirects.

nodes.name: work-items.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the workItemTools catalog of AI assistant tool definitions for work-item (ticket) operations on boards, each with a JSON input schema consumed by the chat agent's tool registry.

nodes.name: tool-filter.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for filterToolsByScope, verifying that chat-bot tool scopes (none / read-only / full) admit or reject the right subsets of the cosmosTools catalog.

nodes.name: tool-filter.ts
nodes.summary: Filters the AI tool catalog by a chat-bot tool scope: classifies tools as read-only via an explicit allowlist plus name-prefix heuristics, and exposes filterToolsByScope to restrict what a scoped bot may call.

nodes.name: classifier.test.ts
nodes.summary: Small unit test for classifyLikelyCui, checking that CUI-like text is flagged and benign text is not.

nodes.name: markings.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for detectMarkings, asserting that classification banner strings (e.g. CUI, SECRET markings) are detected in plain values and nested objects while unmarked content passes.

nodes.name: classifier.ts
nodes.summary: Heuristic CUI classifier: embeds input text and compares it against cached embeddings of CUI seed phrases with cosine similarity to decide whether content is likely Controlled Unclassified Information.
nodes.languageNotes: Seed embeddings are computed lazily once and memoized in a module-level promise, so repeated classifications reuse them.

nodes.name: effective.ts
nodes.summary: Computes the effective data-classification ceiling for an org/project by ranking classification levels, querying DataClassification rows via Prisma, and taking the maximum applicable level.

nodes.name: markings.ts
nodes.summary: Detects explicit classification markings (CUI/secret banner patterns) in arbitrary values by JSON-stringifying them and testing against a marking regex.

nodes.name: dedup-gate.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for dedupGate, covering family exclusion, prefilter thresholds, and that the judge callback only runs on the shortlisted candidates.

nodes.name: dedup-gate.ts
nodes.summary: Two-stage duplicate gate: excludes same-family candidates and applies the cheap token-overlap prefilter, then hands the surviving shortlist to an async judge (typically an LLM) for the final duplicate verdict.

nodes.name: filterToolsByScope
nodes.summary: Returns the subset of tool definitions a chat bot may use for a given scope: empty for none, read-only tools (allowlist plus prefix heuristics) for read scope, or the full catalog otherwise.

nodes.name: classifyLikelyCui
nodes.summary: Embeds the given text and the CUI seed phrases, then returns whether the best cosine similarity crosses the CUI-likeness threshold along with the score.

nodes.name: rankOf
nodes.summary: Maps a classification level string to its numeric rank in the severity order.

nodes.name: maxByRank
nodes.summary: Returns whichever of two classification levels has the higher rank, treating missing values as the base level.

nodes.name: effectiveCeiling
nodes.summary: Loads DataClassification rows for an org (and optional project) via Prisma and computes the highest-ranked applicable classification level as the effective ceiling.

nodes.name: detectMarkings
nodes.summary: JSON-stringifies an arbitrary value and tests it against the classification-marking regex, returning whether explicit CUI/secret banner markings are present.

nodes.name: dedupGate
nodes.summary: Runs the duplicate-detection funnel: filters out same-family candidates, prefilters by token overlap against a threshold, and delegates the shortlist to the injected async judge for the final verdict.

nodes.name: dedup.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the dedup primitives, checking title normalization and token-overlap scoring behavior.

nodes.name: dedup.ts
nodes.summary: Dependency-free duplicate-detection primitives: title normalization, stop-word-aware tokenization, Jaccard-style token overlap scoring, family exclusion for parent/child refs, and a threshold prefilter that shortlists candidates best-first.

nodes.name: guardrails.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the feedback guardrail scanner, exercising prompt-injection and secret detector categories, risk scoring, hold decisions, and secret redaction on crafted feedback payloads.

nodes.name: guardrails.ts
nodes.summary: Regex-based security guardrails for user-submitted feedback: a large detector catalog (prompt injection, jailbreaks, secrets, high-risk zones), scanFeedback scoring and hold/flag decisions, secret redaction, and delimiting of untrusted feedback text before it reaches an LLM.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately dependency-free so it can run in any context; detectors are data (regex + label + weight) evaluated uniformly, and delimitUntrustedFeedback wraps content in explicit UNTRUSTED fences with an instruction preamble.

nodes.name: intake-decision.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for describeIntakeDecision, verifying that guardrail flags, duplicate merges, throttles, and delivered states on feedback automation metadata map to the expected decision descriptions.

nodes.name: intake-decision.ts
nodes.summary: Translates a feedback item's stored automation metadata into a human-readable intake decision (flagged, duplicate, throttled, or delivered) with reason, score, and categories for display in the feedback portal.

nodes.name: intake-guardrails.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for intake guardrails, covering low-quality detection (gibberish, keyboard runs, repeated chars), the LLM dedup judge's tool-use parsing and shortlist validation, and scope judging with mocked model-turn dependencies.

nodes.name: intake-guardrails.ts
nodes.summary: LLM-assisted intake guardrails for the feedback pipeline: heuristic low-quality detection, an LLM duplicate judge built on the dedup gate, an in/out-of-scope judge, and helpers that convert each verdict into a standard intake result record.
nodes.languageNotes: Model calls go through injected deps (runTurn/getCreds) rather than direct imports, keeping the judges unit-testable, and all feedback text is fenced via delimitUntrustedFeedback before reaching the model.

nodes.name: intake-policy.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for intake policy reading, serialization, and input normalization, including defaults, invalid values, and role/zone filtering.

nodes.name: intake-policy.ts
nodes.summary: Assembles the org-level feedback intake policy from org settings JSON: rate limits, role gating, security-classifier configuration, and high-risk zone selection, with serialization and input normalization for the settings API.

nodes.name: rate-limits.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for intake rate limiting, covering limit parsing from settings, duplicate-signature suppression, per-user and per-run caps, backlog caps, and build-cost budgets in planIntake.

nodes.name: rate-limits.ts
nodes.summary: Feedback intake rate limiting: parses org-configured caps (per run, per user, backlog, build-cost budget), computes duplicate signatures, and planIntake partitions candidate items into admitted vs throttled with per-reason messages.

nodes.name: remediate.test.ts
nodes.summary: Large integration test suite for runFeedbackRemediation against a real Prisma database: seeds orgs/projects/boards and feedback fixtures, then verifies triage delivery, guardrail parking, duplicate merging, throttling, role gating, and automation-config handling end to end.

nodes.name: remediate.ts
nodes.summary: The autonomous feedback remediation pipeline: loads org config and pending feedback, applies rate limits, guardrail scans, security judge, role gating, low-quality and duplicate checks, LLM triage, then transactionally creates work items on target boards and fans out audit logs, realtime events, notifications, and Teams messages.
nodes.languageNotes: runFeedbackRemediation is a ~500-line orchestrator that composes nearly every feedback subsystem; side-effect helpers (park/merge/notify) each write feedback state, audit log, realtime publish, and notification in a consistent pattern.

nodes.name: role-gating.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for feedback role gating, verifying default auto-trigger roles, config parsing from settings, per-role auto-trigger decisions, and gate messages.

nodes.name: normalizeTitle
nodes.summary: Lowercases a title, strips bracketed tags and non-alphanumeric characters, and collapses whitespace to produce a canonical comparison form.

nodes.name: tokenOverlap
nodes.summary: Scores similarity of two titles as the shared-token count divided by the smaller token set size, after normalization and stop-word removal.

nodes.name: excludeFamily
nodes.summary: Removes candidates that share a parent ref with the item being checked, so parent/sibling work items are never treated as duplicates of each other.

nodes.name: prefilter
nodes.summary: Scores every candidate by token overlap with the title, keeps those at or above the threshold, and returns them sorted best-first as the dedup shortlist.

nodes.name: redactSecrets
nodes.summary: Replaces every match of the secret patterns (API keys, tokens, credentials) in a text with redaction placeholders before the text is stored or shown to a model.

nodes.name: scanSecrets
nodes.summary: Tests a text against each secret pattern and returns labeled findings for every credential-like match detected.

nodes.name: scanFeedback
nodes.summary: Runs the full detector catalog (optionally filtered to configured high-risk zones) over feedback title and description, aggregates weighted findings into a risk score and categories, and decides whether the item should be held for review.

nodes.name: delimitUntrustedFeedback
nodes.summary: Redacts secrets from feedback text, neutralizes fence markers, and wraps it in explicit UNTRUSTED delimiters with a preamble instructing the model to treat the content as data, never as instructions.

nodes.name: describeIntakeDecision
nodes.summary: Inspects a feedback item's automation metadata record and returns a typed decision (flagged, duplicate, throttled, delivered, or pending) with a human-readable reason, guardrail score, and categories.

nodes.name: longestKeyboardRun
nodes.summary: Measures the longest run of adjacent keyboard-row characters in a text (e.g. 'asdfgh'), used as a gibberish signal for low-quality feedback detection.

nodes.name: detectLowQuality
nodes.summary: Applies cheap heuristics (minimum length, alphanumeric content, repeated single characters, keyboard runs, test-phrase patterns) to flag feedback as low quality before spending model budget on it.

nodes.name: buildDedupJudge
nodes.summary: Builds the async LLM judge for the dedup gate: resolves model credentials, presents the fenced feedback and shortlist to the model with a forced tool call, and validates that any returned duplicate ref actually exists in the shortlist.

nodes.name: findFeedbackDuplicate
nodes.summary: Runs the dedup gate over candidate work items and feedback using the LLM dedup judge, returning the matched duplicate ref and reason when one is found.

nodes.name: judgeFeedbackScope
nodes.summary: Asks the model (via injected deps) to classify fenced feedback as in-scope, out-of-scope, or unclear through a forced tool call, validating the returned class and normalizing the reason.

nodes.name: lowQualityResult
nodes.summary: Wraps a low-quality finding into the standard guardrail-style intake result used to park the feedback item.

nodes.name: duplicateResult
nodes.summary: Converts a duplicate match (ref plus judge reason) into the standard intake result record marking the item as a duplicate.

nodes.name: scopeResult
nodes.summary: Maps a scope-judge verdict to an intake result: out-of-scope items are parked with the judge's reason while in-scope or unclear verdicts allow the item to proceed.

nodes.name: readClassifier
nodes.summary: Parses the security-classifier section of org settings, validating the enabled flag and minimum-confidence value against the allowed set.

nodes.name: readIntakePolicy
nodes.summary: Composes the full intake policy from org settings by delegating to the limits, role-gate, classifier, and high-risk-zone readers.

nodes.name: serializeIntakePolicy
nodes.summary: Serializes an intake policy back into the settings JSON shape persisted on the organization record.

nodes.name: normalizeIntakePolicyInput
nodes.summary: Validates and normalizes untrusted API input into a well-formed intake policy, filtering roles against the known org-role set and re-reading limits, classifier, and zone values through the strict readers.

nodes.name: readIntakeLimits
nodes.summary: Reads and clamps the four intake caps (per run, per user, backlog, build-cost budget) from org settings, falling back to defaults for missing or invalid values.

nodes.name: estimateBuildCost
nodes.summary: Estimates the delivery cost of a feedback item from its content length, used to enforce the per-run build budget.

nodes.name: duplicateSignature
nodes.summary: Derives a normalized lowercase signature from a feedback item's title and description so identical resubmissions within a run can be throttled cheaply.

nodes.name: planIntake
nodes.summary: Partitions candidate feedback into admitted and throttled sets by applying, in order, duplicate-signature suppression, backlog cap, per-user cap, per-run cap, and the build-cost budget, recording a throttle reason for each rejection.

nodes.name: throttleMessage
nodes.summary: Maps a throttle reason code to the user-facing message shown on throttled feedback items.

nodes.name: resolveDeliveryTarget
nodes.summary: Chooses which enabled project a remediated feedback item should deliver to, preferring the item's own project, then the configured default, then the first enabled project.

nodes.name: heuristicTriage
nodes.summary: Keyword-based fallback triage that classifies a feedback item (bug/feature/etc.) with severity and effort when the LLM triage is unavailable or fails.

nodes.name: triageOne
nodes.summary: Triage of a single feedback item via a model turn: sends fenced, secret-redacted feedback plus telemetry through the egress-gated runModelTurn with a forced triage tool, validates severity/effort/acceptance criteria, and falls back to heuristicTriage on any failure.

nodes.name: resolveTypeId
nodes.summary: Resolves the work-item type id to use for a triaged classification by probing the project template's types with a series of Prisma lookups and sensible fallbacks.

nodes.name: buildDescription
nodes.summary: Assembles the created work item's description from the fenced original feedback, triage rationale, acceptance criteria, and author attribution lines.

nodes.name: runFeedbackRemediation
nodes.summary: Orchestrates a full remediation run for an org: loads automation config, intake policy, and pending feedback; applies rate-limit planning, guardrail scans, security judge, role gating, low-quality and duplicate gates; triages survivors with the LLM; and transactionally creates work items with sequenced keys, then emits audit logs, realtime events, notifications, and a Teams summary.

nodes.name: evaluateIntake
nodes.summary: Runs the per-item intake evaluation sequence — duplicate detection then scope judging — returning the first blocking result or clearance to proceed to triage.

nodes.name: mergeDuplicateFeedback
nodes.summary: Transactionally merges a duplicate feedback item into its match: moves non-conflicting votes, marks the duplicate merged with metadata, then logs audit, publishes a realtime event, and notifies the author.

nodes.name: notifyThrottledFeedback
nodes.summary: Marks a feedback item as throttled with its reason, then records the audit entry, publishes the realtime update, and sends the author a notification with the throttle message.

nodes.name: parkForHumanTriage
nodes.summary: Parks a feedback item whose author's role is not allowed to auto-trigger remediation, recording role-gate metadata and emitting audit, realtime, and notification side effects with the role-gate message.

nodes.name: parkFlaggedFeedback
nodes.summary: Parks a guardrail-flagged feedback item for human review: stores the findings, score, and categories in metadata, then logs audit, publishes the realtime event, and notifies org admins of the security hold.

nodes.name: role-gating.ts
nodes.summary: Defines the canonical org role list and role-gating configuration for the feedback portal, determining which organization roles are allowed to auto-trigger feedback remediation.

nodes.name: readRoleGateConfig
nodes.summary: Parses untyped org settings JSON into a validated role-gate config, falling back to the default auto-trigger roles when values are missing or invalid.

nodes.name: canRoleAutoTrigger
nodes.summary: Checks whether a given org role is permitted to auto-trigger feedback remediation under the supplied role-gate config.

nodes.name: roleGateMessage
nodes.summary: Returns the user-facing explanation shown when a submitter's role is gated from auto-triggering remediation.

nodes.name: security-judge.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the feedback security judge, using mocked model turns and credential providers to verify verdict parsing, confidence thresholds, and guardrail escalation via raiseWithJudge.

nodes.name: security-judge.ts
nodes.summary: LLM-based security judge that wraps untrusted feedback in delimiters, runs a model turn to detect prompt injection or malicious intent, and escalates heuristic guardrail scans with the judge's verdict.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses dependency injection for the model-turn runner and credential resolver so tests can stub the LLM boundary.

nodes.name: judgeFeedbackSecurity
nodes.summary: Resolves model credentials, sends delimited untrusted feedback through a model turn, and parses the tool-use response into a structured security verdict with confidence.

nodes.name: raiseWithJudge
nodes.summary: Merges a heuristic guardrail scan result with the judge's verdict, raising the risk level and appending a normalized reason when the judge flags the feedback with sufficient confidence.

nodes.name: propose.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for proposeItems, mocking the Prisma client and model-turn runner to verify document-block prompting and work-item proposal parsing.

nodes.name: propose.ts
nodes.summary: Runs an AI model turn over an ingested document's text blocks to propose work items (issues or milestones), anchoring each proposal back to a source block anchor.

nodes.name: proposeItems
nodes.summary: Loads a document's blocks and the org's tenant context, prompts the model with anchored block text, and sanitizes the tool-use output into capped, anchor-validated item proposals.

nodes.name: config-secrets.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for splitConfigSecrets, verifying that secret-marked provider config fields are separated from plain config values.

nodes.name: config-secrets.ts
nodes.summary: Splits submitted integration configuration into plain config and secret values based on which fields the provider's registry descriptor marks as secret, so secrets can be vault-sealed separately.

nodes.name: splitConfigSecrets
nodes.summary: Partitions a submitted config object into non-secret config and a secret bundle keyed by the provider descriptor's secret-flagged fields.

nodes.name: credentials.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the connector-credential store, covering org/user credential lookup precedence, seal/open round-trips, upserts, and deletion.

nodes.name: credentials.ts
nodes.summary: Encrypted connector-credential store: seals and opens secret bundles through the crypto vault and persists them per org, user, and provider via the Prisma ConnectorCredential model.
nodes.languageNotes: Credentials are stored as vault-sealed JSON bundles; lookups prefer user-scoped credentials before falling back to org-scoped ones.

nodes.name: getCredential
nodes.summary: Fetches the best-matching connector credential for an org/provider (preferring the user's own), decrypting the sealed bundle before returning it.

nodes.name: getUserCredential
nodes.summary: Fetches and decrypts a user-scoped credential bundle for a provider, independent of org.

nodes.name: hasUserCredential
nodes.summary: Cheaply checks whether a user has any stored credential for a provider without decrypting it.

nodes.name: getOrgCredential
nodes.summary: Fetches and decrypts the org-scoped (userId null) credential bundle for a provider.

nodes.name: setCredential
nodes.summary: Seals a credential bundle with the vault and upserts it as a user-scoped ConnectorCredential row, updating in place when one already exists.

nodes.name: setOrgCredential
nodes.summary: Seals a credential bundle and upserts it as the org-scoped credential row for a provider.

nodes.name: deleteOrgCredential
nodes.summary: Deletes all org-scoped credential rows for a provider.

nodes.name: filter.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the integrations catalog filtering and category-grouping helpers.

nodes.name: filter.ts
nodes.summary: Pure helpers for the integrations catalog UI: text/category filtering of provider descriptors and grouping providers into labeled category buckets.

nodes.name: filterProviders
nodes.summary: Filters provider descriptors by an optional category and a case-insensitive text query over name, description, and category.

nodes.name: groupByCategory
nodes.summary: Buckets provider descriptors by category and returns sorted groups with human-readable labels from CATEGORY_META.

nodes.name: microsoft-graph.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the Microsoft Graph client, using a mocked fetch to verify token minting, caching, cloud endpoint selection, and Graph request/upload/download behavior.

nodes.name: microsoft-graph.ts

nodes.name: endpointsFor

nodes.name: resolveGraphAccess

nodes.name: getGraphToken
nodes.summary: Mints a client-credentials OAuth token for the org's Microsoft cloud, caching it per org until near expiry and surfacing detailed error messages on failure.

nodes.name: graphFetch

nodes.name: graphUploadFile
nodes.summary: Uploads binary content to a Graph drive path (e.g. SharePoint) using a PUT request with the org's token.

nodes.name: graphDownloadFile
nodes.summary: Downloads a file from a Graph path for an org, returning the raw bytes and content type.

nodes.name: nango.test.ts

nodes.name: nangoEnabled
nodes.summary: Reports whether Nango integration is enabled based on the secret-key environment variable.

nodes.name: createConnectSession
nodes.summary: Creates a Nango connect session for an org/provider pair so the frontend can launch the OAuth flow, returning the session token.

nodes.name: listConnections
nodes.summary: Lists an org's active Nango connections, returning an empty list when Nango is disabled.

nodes.name: getConnection
nodes.summary: Fetches a single org/provider Nango connection, returning null when disabled or not found.

nodes.name: getNangoToken
nodes.summary: Retrieves the current OAuth access token for an org/provider connection from Nango.

nodes.name: nangoProxy
nodes.summary: Proxies an HTTP request to a third-party API through Nango using the org/provider connection, normalizing the response and errors.

nodes.name: registry.test.ts

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.name: teams-notify-config.ts

nodes.name: teams-notify.ts

nodes.name: teamsEventEnabled

nodes.name: teamsNotify

nodes.name: teams.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the Teams Graph messaging client, using a scripted fake fetch to verify token minting, channel message posting, and connection testing.

nodes.name: teams.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Accepts an injectable fetch implementation so tests can script token and Graph responses without network access.

nodes.name: resolveConfig
nodes.summary: Combines the org's vault-stored Teams credential with its integration row to produce the client id/secret, tenant, cloud, and target team/channel configuration.

nodes.name: mintToken
nodes.summary: Requests a client-credentials OAuth token from the cloud-appropriate login endpoint for the resolved Teams config, decoding token errors into readable messages.

nodes.name: postTeamsChannelMessage
nodes.summary: Posts an HTML-formatted message to the org's configured Teams team/channel via the Graph chatMessages endpoint, minting a token first and reporting structured errors.

nodes.name: testTeamsConnection
nodes.summary: Validates an org's Teams setup by resolving its config and attempting to mint a token, returning a success flag with error detail.

nodes.name: metrics.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite verifying that egress and classifier metric recorders emit counters and histograms with the expected attributes.

nodes.name: metrics.ts
nodes.summary: Observability instrumentation for the AI egress layer: defines counters and a latency histogram, and exposes recorders for egress decisions, egress errors, and classifier invocations, latency, and errors.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses OpenTelemetry-style meter instruments created at module scope so all recorders share the same counters.

nodes.name: recordEgressDecision
nodes.summary: Increments the egress-decision counter with attributes describing the decision outcome and context.

nodes.name: recordEgressError
nodes.summary: Increments the egress-error counter tagged with the pipeline stage where the failure occurred.

nodes.name: recordClassifier
nodes.summary: Records a classifier invocation, incrementing the invocation counter and recording its latency histogram sample.

nodes.name: recordClassifierError
nodes.summary: Records a failed classifier invocation by incrementing both the error and invocation counters.

nodes.name: guardrails.test.ts

nodes.name: applyGovGuardrails
nodes.summary: Removes commercial-only connector providers from an org's stored runtime config via upsert, enforcing GovCloud tenant restrictions.

nodes.name: govGuardrailViolation
nodes.summary: Checks a runtime-config patch against the tenant class and returns a violation message listing any commercial-only providers a GovCloud tenant attempts to enable.

nodes.name: index.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for runtime-config loading, verifying defaults are returned when no row exists and stored rows are normalized correctly.

nodes.name: index.ts
nodes.summary: Per-org runtime configuration loader: defines the default runtime config and fetches an org's OrgRuntimeConfig row from Prisma, normalizing it against defaults.

nodes.name: getRuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Loads an org's runtime config row from the database and returns it normalized, falling back to defaults when absent.

nodes.name: normalizeRuntimeConfig
nodes.summary: Merges a raw OrgRuntimeConfig row with the default runtime config, coercing nullable fields into a fully-populated config object.

nodes.name: pastTenseLabel

nodes.summary: Lightweight popover grid of preset emoji used to add reactions to chat messages.

nodes.name: MarkdownContent

nodes.summary: Exported component mapping messages to MessageItem rows with time grouping, mention resolution via useRefResolver, and end-of-list read receipts.

nodes.summary: Side panel listing a channel's pinned messages via the usePinnedMessages hook, with unpin and jump-to-message actions.

nodes.name: PinnedPanel
nodes.summary: Exported panel component rendering pinned message previews with author and unpin controls.

nodes.name: reaction-bar.tsx
nodes.summary: Row of grouped emoji reaction pills under a chat message, highlighting the current user's reactions and toggling them on click.

nodes.summary: Exported component aggregating message reactions by emoji into count pills and invoking a toggle callback.

nodes.name: ReadReceiptAvatars

nodes.summary: Autocomplete dropdown for chat slash commands, filtering the shared COMMANDS registry and supporting keyboard selection from the composer.

nodes.summary: Small presence widget showing which members are currently typing in the channel with animated dots.

nodes.summary: Docked-drawer panel embedding the chat experience outside the dedicated chat page: channel list via ChatSidebar and the selected channel's ChannelView, with local channel selection state.

nodes.summary: Floating picker for @-entity mentions used by the chat composer and assistant panel; searches entities as the user types, groups results by entity type with icons, and supports keyboard navigation and selection.

nodes.name: EntityMentionPicker
nodes.summary: Exported picker component driven by useEntitySearch that positions itself near the caret, orders results by ENTITY_ORDER, and emits the chosen entity ref.

nodes.name: useRefResolver

nodes.name: markdown.test.ts

nodes.name: mentionTransformer
nodes.summary: Text-match transformer converting between mention token syntax in markdown and MentionNode instances in the Lexical tree.

nodes.name: notesTransformers
nodes.summary: Exported helper returning the full transformer list (standard Lexical transformers plus the mention transformer) for the notes editor.

nodes.name: mention-node.ts
nodes.summary: Custom Lexical node representing an inline entity mention in notes, storing entity type and id, rendering a styled DOM chip, and supporting JSON import/export plus factory and type-guard helpers.

nodes.summary: TextNode subclass carrying entityType and id, overriding clone, createDOM, importJSON/exportJSON, and text-entity insertion rules so mentions behave as atomic tokens.

nodes.name: $createMentionNode
nodes.summary: Factory that constructs a MentionNode in segmented, non-editable token mode for a given entity ref.

nodes.name: $isMentionNode
nodes.summary: Type guard checking whether a Lexical node is a MentionNode.

nodes.name: NoteRichTextEditor
nodes.summary: Exported editor component configuring LexicalComposer with custom nodes, plugins, theme, and markdown-based onChange serialization for note content.

nodes.name: logTime
nodes.summary: Validates input and creates a TimeEntry record for a work item after asserting the actor's time-logging permission.

nodes.name: listTimeEntries
nodes.summary: Lists time entries with filters and a capped page size, returning entries plus total hours computed via reduce.

nodes.name: utility.ts
nodes.summary: Implements the fetch_url AI tool: SSRF-guarded URL fetching (via webhook URL schema), byte-capped streaming reads with abort, and HTML-to-plain-text stripping for model consumption.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a streaming reader with an AbortController to cap response size instead of trusting Content-Length.

nodes.name: stripHtmlToText
nodes.summary: Strips scripts, styles, comments and tags from HTML and decodes common entities to produce whitespace-normalized plain text.

nodes.name: readCapped
nodes.summary: Reads a fetch response body via streaming reader up to a byte cap, aborting the request and truncating once the limit is reached.

nodes.name: fetchUrl
nodes.summary: Exported fetch_url tool executor: validates the URL against the SSRF-safe schema, fetches with a timeout, caps the body, and converts HTML responses to plain text.

nodes.name: work-items.test.ts

nodes.name: work-items.ts

nodes.languageNotes: Uses Prisma interactive transactions to compute per-project ordering and sequence numbers atomically on create.

nodes.name: resolveWorkItemTypeId
nodes.summary: Resolves a work-item type from either a UUID or a fuzzy type name, scoped to the project's template, falling back to partial name matching.

nodes.name: createWorkItem
nodes.summary: Creates a work item in a transaction with computed sort order and sequence number, records an activity, converts calendar dates to noon UTC, and fires off embedding storage.

nodes.name: updateWorkItem
nodes.summary: Updates a work item's fields, detects done-column moves to set completion, syncs linked feedback status, and refreshes the item's embedding.

nodes.name: deleteWorkItem
nodes.summary: Deletes a work item after verifying it belongs to the actor's org and the actor holds the delete permission.

nodes.name: listWorkItems
nodes.summary: Lists work items with filters (project, assignee, column, type) and a capped limit, resolving type names to IDs first.

nodes.name: listItemLinks
nodes.summary: Lists work-item dependency/relation links for a project after validating org ownership.

nodes.name: linkItems
nodes.summary: Creates a typed link between two work items, rejecting duplicates and refusing links whose directed dependency edge would create a cycle.

nodes.name: unlinkItems
nodes.summary: Removes an existing work-item link after validating input and locating the link within the org.

nodes.name: tool-executor.test.ts

nodes.summary: Extracts structured tool calls from raw model output text by scanning for tool-call markers and JSON-parsing their payloads, warning on malformed blocks.

nodes.name: executeTool

nodes.name: dispatchTool
nodes.summary: Giant switch that maps every supported tool name to its executor function across all domain modules, delegating connector tools to the connector registry.

nodes.name: auditAssistantToolUse
nodes.summary: Best-effort audit logging of each assistant tool invocation, summarizing arguments and extracting an entity id from the result without failing the tool call.

nodes.name: queryWorkItems
nodes.summary: Inline read-only tool that queries work items with filters and a capped limit after asserting read permission.

nodes.name: queryIntervals
nodes.summary: Inline tool that lists project intervals (sprints/PIs) with filters and a capped limit.

nodes.name: queryCrm
nodes.summary: Inline tool that queries CRM contacts, canonicalizing the pipeline stage filter before hitting Prisma.

nodes.name: queryFinance
nodes.summary: Inline tool that fetches revenues and expenses in parallel and computes totals and net using Decimal money helpers.

nodes.name: generateIntervalBrief
nodes.summary: Builds a progress brief for an interval: completed vs. total points, elapsed-time percentage, and a list of blocked or overdue items.

nodes.name: stages.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for CRM stage constants, schema validation and stage-filter canonicalization.

nodes.name: canonicalizeStageFilter
nodes.summary: Normalizes a user-supplied stage string to the canonical uppercase stage key, or undefined if unknown.

nodes.name: posting.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests asserting that invoice and payment posting lines are balanced (debits equal credits) across tax and no-tax scenarios.

nodes.name: invoicingAccounts
nodes.summary: Resolves the accounts-receivable, revenue, tax-payable and cash accounts for an org in parallel from the chart of accounts.

nodes.name: paymentToPostingLines
nodes.summary: Maps an invoice payment to posting lines debiting cash and crediting accounts receivable.

nodes.name: postInvoiceToLedger
nodes.summary: Posts a journal entry for an invoice using resolved invoicing accounts and the generated posting lines.

nodes.name: postPaymentToLedger
nodes.summary: Posts a journal entry for an invoice payment using the cash/AR posting lines.

nodes.name: reverseInvoiceLedger

nodes.name: totals.test.ts

nodes.name: lineAmount
nodes.summary: Computes a rounded line amount as quantity times unit price.

nodes.name: lineTax
nodes.summary: Computes the rounded tax for a line amount given a percentage tax rate.

nodes.name: invoiceTotals
nodes.summary: Aggregates invoice lines into subtotal, tax total and grand total using Decimal summation.

nodes.summary: Derives the invoice status (e.g. paid or partially paid) by comparing the amount paid against the total, preserving the current status otherwise.

nodes.name: postRevenueToLedger
nodes.summary: Posts a journal entry for a revenue record by resolving standard accounts and mapping the revenue to posting lines.

nodes.name: postExpenseToLedger
nodes.summary: Posts a journal entry for an expense record by resolving standard accounts and mapping the expense to posting lines.

nodes.name: safeAutoPost
nodes.summary: Runs an auto-posting function and swallows errors with a console log so ledger failures never break the primary finance write path.

nodes.name: chart-of-accounts.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests validating the default chart of accounts definitions (codes, types and normal balances).

nodes.name: seedSystemCoA
nodes.summary: Bulk-creates the default system chart of accounts for an org, skipping duplicates.

nodes.name: resolveAccount
nodes.summary: Looks up an org account by code, seeding the system chart of accounts and retrying if the account does not yet exist.

nodes.name: mappers.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests checking that revenue and expense records map to balanced double-entry posting lines.

nodes.name: mappers.ts

nodes.name: revenueToPostingLines
nodes.summary: Maps a revenue record to posting lines debiting cash and crediting revenue.

nodes.name: expenseToPostingLines
nodes.summary: Maps an expense record to posting lines debiting the expense account and crediting cash.

nodes.summary: Seeds the chart of accounts and posts journal entries for every historical revenue and expense not yet in the ledger, collecting per-record errors and returning posted/failed counts.

nodes.name: posting.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the journal posting engine's balance assertion and line reversal helpers.

nodes.name: assertBalanced
nodes.summary: Throws unless all line amounts are positive and total debits exactly equal total credits.

nodes.name: reversedLines
nodes.summary: Produces mirror posting lines with debit and credit directions swapped.

nodes.name: ClosedPeriodError
nodes.summary: Error subclass raised when a posting targets a date inside a closed accounting period.

nodes.name: postEntry

nodes.name: branchScopeWhere
nodes.summary: Converts a resolved branch scope into a Prisma where-clause fragment for filtering branch-scoped records.

nodes.name: builtin-work-roles-seed.test.ts

nodes.name: seedBuiltinWorkRoles
nodes.summary: Upserts every built-in work role for the given org, converting each role's permission keys to a database mask and marking rows as isBuiltIn.

nodes.name: builtin-work-roles.test.ts

nodes.name: check.ts

nodes.name: requirePermission
nodes.summary: Asserts that an auth context holds a required permission, throwing ForbiddenError when the check fails.

nodes.name: ForbiddenError
nodes.summary: Error class signalling a 403 authorization failure, thrown by permission guards and caught by the shared API error handler.

nodes.name: NotFoundError
nodes.summary: Error class signalling a 404 missing-resource condition, used by service and route code and mapped by the API error handler.

nodes.name: ConflictError
nodes.summary: Error class signalling a 409 conflict (e.g. duplicate resource), mapped to an HTTP response by the shared API error handler.

nodes.name: effective-permissions.ts
nodes.summary: Loads a user's full effective authorization state for an org in one query: base role permissions, work-role permission masks OR'd in, and the combined ABAC rule set from all assigned work roles.

nodes.name: loadEffectivePermissions
nodes.summary: Fetches an org member with their work-role assignments and combines role defaults, stored overrides, and work-role masks into one permission bitmask plus the merged ABAC rule list.

nodes.name: permissions.test.ts
nodes.summary: Unit tests for the permission bitmask system: hasPermission/hasAnyPermission semantics, role default masks, override resolution via resolvePermissions, and mask serialization round-trips.

nodes.name: permissions.ts
nodes.summary: Foundation of the RBAC system: defines every permission as a BigInt bit flag (org, project, board, item, sprint, finance, and more), per-role default masks, and helpers for combining, checking, serializing, and naming permission masks. Imported by dozens of API routes, services, and UI components.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses TypeScript BigInt literals (1n << Nn) so the permission space can exceed 32 bits safely; masks are stored in the database as decimal strings via maskToDb/maskFromDb.

nodes.name: maskFromDb
nodes.summary: Parses a permission mask stored in the database (string form) back into a BigInt bitmask.

nodes.name: maskToDb
nodes.summary: Serializes a BigInt permission mask to its database string representation.

nodes.name: hasPermission
nodes.summary: Checks whether a user's permission bitmask includes all bits of a required permission.

nodes.name: hasAnyPermission
nodes.summary: Returns true when a user's permission bitmask satisfies at least one of the listed required permissions.

nodes.name: getEffectivePermissions
nodes.summary: Derives an effective mask from a role's defaults with an optional explicit override mask taking precedence.

nodes.name: permissionNames
nodes.summary: Expands a permission bitmask into the list of human-readable permission key names it contains.

nodes.name: permissionMaskFromKeys
nodes.summary: Builds a permission bitmask from a list of permission key names, ignoring unknown keys.

nodes.name: isPermissionSubset
nodes.summary: Checks whether one permission mask is entirely contained within another, used to prevent privilege escalation when granting roles.

nodes.name: scope.ts
nodes.summary: Project-level management scoping: determines whether a user can manage a specific project and filters a set of project ids down to those the user manages, combining org-wide PROJECT_MANAGE permission with per-project membership roles.

nodes.name: canManageProject
nodes.summary: Returns whether the auth context can manage a given project, via org-wide manage permission, org admin/owner role, or a managing project-member role.

nodes.name: getManagedProjectIds
nodes.summary: Filters a list of project ids to those the user can manage, short-circuiting for org-wide managers and otherwise querying managing project memberships.

nodes.name: work-role.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the work-role DTO mapper and the zod create/update/policy schemas, covering permission-name expansion, policy validation, and rejection of malformed input.

nodes.name: work-role.ts

nodes.name: toWorkRoleDto
nodes.summary: Converts a WorkRole database row into an API DTO, expanding the permission mask into key names and serializing timestamps.

nodes.name: broker.ts
nodes.summary: Thin org-scoped facade over the realtime bus: publishes typed events to an org topic and subscribes handlers to org events, used by API routes to push live updates (work items, members, feedback) to connected clients.

nodes.name: publishToOrg
nodes.summary: Publishes a typed event payload onto the org's realtime topic via the shared bus.

nodes.name: subscribeToOrg
nodes.summary: Subscribes a handler to an org's realtime topic, serializing bus events to JSON strings and returning an unsubscribe function.

nodes.name: getActiveSubscriberCount
nodes.summary: Reports the number of currently active org subscriptions, used for diagnostics.

nodes.name: image-url.test.ts
nodes.summary: Tests the image URL validation schemas: accepting https/http URLs and size-bounded data:image URIs, rejecting javascript: and other unsafe schemes, and enforcing avatar byte limits.

nodes.name: image-url.ts
nodes.summary: Security-focused zod schemas for user-supplied image URLs (logos, avatars): allows only http(s) URLs or size-limited data:image URIs, blocking javascript: and other injection vectors, with exported avatar size constants.

nodes.name: imageUrlSchema
nodes.summary: Factory producing a nullable/optional zod string schema that accepts http(s) URLs or data:image URIs up to a byte cap, rejecting all other schemes.

nodes.name: webhook-url.ts
nodes.summary: SSRF-protection schema for outbound webhook URLs: rejects private/loopback IPv4 ranges, localhost, and non-http(s) schemes before a webhook target is stored or fetched.

nodes.name: isPrivateIpv4
nodes.summary: Detects whether a host string is a private, loopback, or link-local IPv4 address (10.x, 127.x, 169.254.x, 172.16-31.x, 192.168.x).

nodes.name: index.test.ts

nodes.name: index.ts

nodes.name: getStorage
nodes.summary: Returns the singleton storage adapter, creating a local or S3 adapter on first use based on environment configuration.

nodes.name: service.ts

nodes.summary: Creates a tax rate for an org, clearing any existing default first when the new rate is marked as default.

nodes.name: updateTaxRate

nodes.name: deleteTaxRate

nodes.name: taxLiability

nodes.name: validation.ts
nodes.summary: Zod schemas validating tax-rate create and update payloads (name, percentage rate bounds, default flag) for the tax-rates API routes.

nodes.name: server.ts

nodes.name: serverReportError

nodes.name: slugify.test.ts

nodes.name: use-broadcast-channel-leader.ts

nodes.name: useBroadcastChannelLeader

nodes.name: use-chat-messages.ts

nodes.name: use-chat-presence.ts

nodes.name: useChatPresence

nodes.name: use-chat-read-state.ts

nodes.summary: Reducer over a userId to lastReadMessageId Map, handling bulk seed and single-entry set actions immutably.

nodes.name: useChatReadState
nodes.summary: Fetches initial read-state rows for a channel, dispatches them into the reducer, and returns the map plus a callback to record a user's latest read message.

nodes.name: use-chat-thread.ts
nodes.summary: TanStack Query hook that fetches the reply messages of a chat thread (children of a parent message) for the thread pane.

nodes.name: useChatThread
nodes.summary: Queries /chat/channels/:channelId/messages/:parentMessageId/thread with an org-scoped key, enabled only when a parent message id is present.

nodes.name: use-chat-typing.ts
nodes.summary: Hook managing typing indicators for a chat channel: tracks who is typing with expiry-based pruning on an interval, and throttles POSTs announcing the current user's own typing activity.

nodes.summary: Reducer over a userId to last-typing-timestamp Map that records typing events, prunes expired entries, and clears on channel change.

nodes.name: useChatTyping

nodes.summary: Reducer maintaining the pins array and a derived Set of pinned message ids, handling seed and remove actions.

nodes.name: usePinnedMessages
nodes.summary: Loads a channel's pins on mount and subscribes to realtime events to refetch when pins change or drop entries when messages are deleted.

nodes.name: use-realtime-events.ts

nodes.name: useRealtimeEvents
nodes.summary: Subscribes handler callbacks to org server-sent events; as leader it binds typed listeners for all known server event types on an EventSource and rebroadcasts to followers, otherwise it listens on the BroadcastChannel.

nodes.name: artifacts.test.ts

nodes.name: tool-status.test.ts

nodes.name: message-time.test.ts

nodes.name: delete-user.ts
nodes.summary: Platform-admin user deletion implemented as in-place anonymization: one Prisma transaction revokes all sessions, org memberships, federated identities, push subscriptions, allowlist entries, and invitations, then rewrites the user to a 'Deleted user' tombstone with an RFC-2606 sentinel email. Authored business and financial records stay attributed to the tombstone to avoid orphaning rows guarded by RESTRICT or FK-less author columns.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately avoids a hard row delete: a RESTRICT foreign key on chat_bot_runs and FK-less required author columns across ~20 tables would either fail the delete or silently orphan financial records.

nodes.name: deleteUserAccount
nodes.summary: In one Prisma transaction, deletes the user's sessions, org memberships, federated identities, push subscriptions, allowlist entries, and pending invitations, then anonymizes the user record and frees the original email via a deleted-<id>@deleted.invalid sentinel; returns counts of everything revoked. Performs no authorization itself — callers must enforce the platform-admin guards.

nodes.name: require-system-admin.ts

nodes.name: requireSystemAdmin

nodes.name: seedAec
nodes.summary: Upserts the AEC sector work-item types and their hierarchy into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: consulting.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the consulting sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedConsulting function.

nodes.name: seedConsulting
nodes.summary: Upserts the consulting sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: education.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the education sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedEducation function.

nodes.name: seedEducation
nodes.summary: Upserts the education sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: event.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the event-management sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedEvent function.

nodes.name: seedEvent
nodes.summary: Upserts the event sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: manufacturing.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the manufacturing sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedManufacturing function.

nodes.name: seedManufacturing
nodes.summary: Upserts the manufacturing sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: ops.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the operations sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedOps function.

nodes.name: seedOps
nodes.summary: Upserts the operations sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: software.ts
nodes.summary: Seed module defining the software sector's built-in work-item type taxonomy (epics, stories, bugs, and related types) and inserting it idempotently via the exported seedSoftwareSector function.

nodes.name: seedSoftwareSector
nodes.summary: Upserts the software sector work-item types into the database from the module's static definitions.

nodes.name: cross-cutting.ts
nodes.summary: Seeds the eight cross-sector work-item types shared by every tenant — Goal, Milestone, KPI, Objective, Key Result, Risk, Decision, and Meeting Note — each with key, icon, color, celebration flag, and optional default parent type.

nodes.name: seedCrossCuttingTypes
nodes.summary: Iterates the static cross-cutting type list and upserts each work-item type, wiring the Key Result type to its default Objective parent.

nodes.name: prisma-client.ts
nodes.summary: Shared factory building a PrismaClient for all seed and CLI scripts using the Prisma 7 PrismaPg driver adapter, with an optional explicit connection string falling back to DATABASE_URL.
nodes.languageNotes: Prisma 7 requires a driver adapter — the connection URL no longer lives in schema.prisma, so PrismaPg opens the node-postgres pool here.

nodes.name: makePrismaClient
nodes.summary: Returns a PrismaClient wired to a PrismaPg adapter, targeting the given connection string or DATABASE_URL.

nodes.name: test-fixtures.ts
nodes.summary: Idempotent seed for E2E test fixtures used by the H2 Playwright spec: creates the 'test-org' organization, alice (ADMIN) and bob (MEMBER) test users joined to the org and auto-joined to #general, plus a project fixture, a second board, a built-in task type, and mention fixtures.

nodes.name: ensureGeneralChannel
nodes.summary: Creates the org's #general chat channel if it does not already exist and returns it.

nodes.name: autoJoinGeneral
nodes.summary: Joins a test user to the #general channel, mirroring the app's auto-join behavior for new members.

nodes.name: ensureProjectFixture
nodes.summary: Creates or reuses the E2E project fixture with its default board and columns inside the test org.

nodes.name: ensureSecondBoard
nodes.summary: Ensures the fixture project has a second board so board-switching flows can be exercised in tests.

nodes.name: ensureBuiltInTaskType
nodes.summary: Ensures a built-in Task work-item type exists so work items can be created during E2E runs.

nodes.name: ensureMentionFixtures
nodes.summary: Seeds the chat messages and mention rows needed by the mention-notification E2E scenarios.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Creates the test org and alice/bob users, joins them to the org and #general, then runs the project, board, task-type, and mention fixture builders.

nodes.name: wire-keycloak-idp.ts
nodes.summary: CLI script that wires a Keycloak OIDC identity provider onto an existing org by upserting its single IdpConnection (one-IdP-per-org unique constraint), pointing it at a Keycloak realm's OIDC discovery base. The client secret is sealed with the crypto/vault keyring before it touches the database, and re-running rotates the secret and refreshes issuer/scopes in place.
nodes.languageNotes: Fully parameterized via environment variables; the org itself is only looked up, never created.

nodes.name: resolveDbUrl
nodes.summary: Resolves the database connection URL for the target deployment from environment configuration.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Looks up the org, seals the Keycloak client secret with the vault keyring, and upserts the IdpConnection on orgId with the realm's issuer, client id, and scopes.

nodes.name: page.tsx
nodes.summary: Server-rendered project import page: resolves the auth context for the org slug (redirecting when unauthenticated), loads the project by key via Prisma, and renders the ImportWizard inside the shared PageShell.

nodes.name: ProjectImportPage
nodes.summary: Async server component that authenticates the request, fetches the project scoped to the org, 404s when missing, and mounts the ImportWizard with the resolved org and project identifiers.

nodes.name: import-wizard.tsx
nodes.summary: Generalized client-side import wizard that opens with a 'What are you importing?' entity picker: choosing Work Items runs the existing WorkItemImportWizard unchanged, while any other entity runs the generic flow (upload, map columns, validate, import) posting { entity, mode, mapping, rows } to the /import endpoint. The generic flow deliberately has no interactive value-mapping step — the server coerces enums tolerantly and reports unrecognized values as per-row warnings.

nodes.name: ImportWizard
nodes.summary: Top-level wizard component that routes between the entity picker, the WorkItemImportWizard, and the generic import flow based on the selected entity.

nodes.name: BackToPicker
nodes.summary: Small navigation control returning the user from a flow back to the entity picker.

nodes.name: EntityPicker
nodes.summary: Card grid listing every importable entity definition and invoking the selection callback with the chosen entity.

nodes.name: GenericImportFlow
nodes.summary: The four-step generic import flow: parses the uploaded workbook, guesses header rows and column-to-field mappings from the entity definition, validates, posts the rows to the project's /import endpoint, and renders the resulting import report with per-row warnings.

nodes.name: chooseDefaultSheet
nodes.summary: Picks the most plausible default worksheet from a parsed workbook by comparing data row counts.

nodes.name: GStepBadge
nodes.summary: Renders the step-progress badge strip for the generic import flow.

nodes.name: Stat
nodes.summary: Displays a labeled count tile in the import report summary.

nodes.name: work-item-import-wizard.tsx
nodes.summary: Client-side multi-step wizard for importing work items from CSV/XLSX files: parses the file, guesses target-field and priority mappings per column, lets the user adjust value maps and defaults, and posts to the project's /work-items/import endpoint with externalId-based idempotency, ending in a summary report.

nodes.name: WorkItemImportWizard
nodes.summary: Main wizard component managing upload, column mapping with guessTarget/guessPriority heuristics, value-map editing, submission to /work-items/import, and the final report view.

nodes.name: StepBadge
nodes.summary: Renders the numbered step-progress indicator for the work-item wizard.

nodes.name: ValueGroup
nodes.summary: Editor for mapping a column's distinct source values onto target values (e.g. status or priority) during import.

nodes.name: Stat
nodes.summary: Displays a labeled count tile in the work-item import report.

nodes.name: convert.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest suite for the document-block conversion pipeline: mocks the storage layer and RAG embedding, ingests fixture documents with ingestDocument, then asserts the block-to-work-item/milestone/table conversions write the expected Prisma records.

nodes.name: ingest.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest test for ingestDocument that mocks the storage backend so no MinIO instance is required, feeding fixture files and asserting the ingested document rows.

nodes.name: convert.ts
nodes.summary: Server-side conversion library turning ingested document blocks into first-class records: single blocks become work items, milestones, objectives, goals, intervals, roadmap nodes, or generic items, and tables become batches of work items. Resolves target types/columns, scopes everything to org and project, and stores RAG embeddings for created items.

nodes.name: resolveTypeAndColumn
nodes.summary: Resolves the work-item type and default board column a converted block should land in for a given project.

nodes.name: convertBlockToWorkItem
nodes.summary: Creates a work item from a single document block's text, linking it back to the source block and placing it on the resolved board column.

nodes.name: convertBlockToMilestone
nodes.summary: Creates a milestone record from a document block, deriving title and body from the block text.

nodes.name: convertTableToWorkItems
nodes.summary: Converts a table block into one work item per data row, mapping table columns onto work-item fields.

nodes.name: convertBlockToObjective
nodes.summary: Creates an OKR objective from a document block within the org/project scope.

nodes.name: convertBlockToGoal
nodes.summary: Creates a delivery goal record from a document block's text.

nodes.name: convertBlockToInterval
nodes.summary: Creates a planning interval (e.g. sprint/PI) from a document block, parsing any date hints from the text.

nodes.name: convertBlockToRoadmapNode
nodes.summary: Creates a roadmap node from a document block, using roadmapSlug to key it into the project's roadmap.

nodes.name: convertBlockToItem
nodes.summary: Creates a generic item from a document block and stores a RAG embedding for the new record.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route exposing the current user's Google Calendar: GET lists upcoming events and POST creates an event via the per-user Google OAuth client, with rate limiting and a 428 hint when Google is not connected.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Lists the user's upcoming Google Calendar events within an optional time window, returning a not-connected error when no Google token exists.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Creates a Google Calendar event from the request body using the user's OAuth-backed calendar client.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route listing the current user's Google Drive files through the per-user OAuth Drive client, with rate limiting, optional search query, and a not-connected fallback error.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Lists Google Drive files for the authenticated user with optional query and page-size limits.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route listing the current user's recent Gmail messages: fetches message ids then hydrates headers/snippets in parallel via the per-user Gmail client.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Lists recent Gmail messages, fetching metadata for each id in parallel and filtering failed lookups.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Slash-command dispatcher for a chat channel: handles /topic, /invite, /kick, /leave, /mute, /ai and /notes, enforcing channel management rules, posting system messages, and detaching AI bot runs.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Parses and executes a slash command against the channel: mutates topic/membership, posts server messages, publishes realtime events, and fires runChatBot for /ai and /notes without awaiting.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route letting an org member join a public chat channel; rejects private/DM channels and publishes a channels-updated event to the joining user.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Upserts the caller as a member of a public channel and notifies them via the realtime bus.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route letting a member leave a chat channel; blocks leaving the general channel and DMs, then removes membership and publishes a realtime update.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Deletes the caller's channel membership (guarding general/DM channels) and publishes a channels-updated event.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route for removing a specific member from a chat channel; requires channel-manage rights, refuses to remove the last member, and notifies the removed user in realtime.

nodes.name: DELETE
nodes.summary: Removes a user from a channel after manage-permission and last-member checks, then publishes a realtime update to the removed user.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route for chat channel membership: GET returns the sorted member roster with display names, POST bulk-adds org members to the channel for users with manage rights.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Lists channel members joined with user display names and avatars, sorted alphabetically.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Validates that all requested userIds are org members, bulk-inserts channel memberships, and notifies each added user over the realtime bus.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Core chat message route: GET pages message history (with reactions, attachments, and reply counts) and POST creates a message, then detaches an AI bot run when the message mentions a bot and the sender has AI permission.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Returns the latest messages for a channel in chronological order with cursor-based pagination, gated by channel visibility.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Creates a user message via createUserMessage (idempotent on clientMsgId), then resolves any bot mention and fires runChatBot without awaiting.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route to unpin a message from a chat channel, publishing a pin-removed realtime event to channel subscribers.

nodes.name: DELETE
nodes.summary: Deletes the pinned-message record for a channel (idempotent) and broadcasts chat.pin.removed.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route for channel pins: GET lists pinned messages with pinner/author info, POST pins a message (max 50 per channel), broadcasts the pin event, and posts a system message.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Lists a channel's pinned messages including message content and the user who pinned each.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Pins a message after visibility, existence, and per-channel cap checks, publishes chat.pin.added, and posts a server message announcing the pin.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route recording a user's read position in a channel: updates lastReadMessageId/lastReadAt and publishes read-state events to both the reader and the channel.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Persists the caller's last-read message for the channel and emits chat.read realtime events.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route broadcasting a typing indicator for a channel over the realtime bus; heavily rate-limited and gated on post permission, with no persistence.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Publishes a chat.typing event with the caller's identity and an expiry timestamp after access and rate-limit checks.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Chat channel collection route: GET returns the caller's channels/DMs with unread counts and DM participant info; POST creates a channel (slug validation, optional privacy, project linking, initial members) in a transaction with audit logging.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Builds the caller's channel list from their memberships, enriching DMs and group DMs with the other participants' names and avatars.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Creates a chat channel and its initial memberships in one transaction, validating the slug, member ids, and optional project link, then audits and notifies members.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route that opens (or returns the existing) direct-message channel for a set of users, using a deterministic sorted-participants DM key to deduplicate conversations.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Finds an existing DM/group-DM by its canonical participant key or creates one transactionally, then notifies all participants.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route removing the caller's emoji reaction from a chat message and broadcasting a reaction-removed event to the message's channel.

nodes.name: DELETE
nodes.summary: Deletes the caller's reaction for the decoded emoji (idempotent) and publishes chat.reaction.removed.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: API route adding an emoji reaction to a chat message: validates channel visibility, upserts the reaction, and broadcasts a reaction-added event, with rate limiting.

nodes.name: POST
nodes.summary: Upserts the caller's emoji reaction on a message after access checks and publishes chat.reaction.added.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Single chat message route: PATCH lets the author edit their message within an edit window, DELETE soft-deletes a message by the author or a channel manager, both broadcasting realtime updates.

nodes.name: PATCH
nodes.summary: Edits a message's content (author-only) and publishes chat.message.updated with the edited flag.

nodes.name: DELETE
nodes.summary: Soft-deletes a message when allowed by canDeleteMessageGiven (author or manager) and publishes chat.message.deleted.

nodes.name: route.ts
nodes.summary: Server-Sent Events endpoint streaming realtime org events: subscribes the caller to org, user, and member-channel topics on the bus, tracks presence with heartbeats, and cleans up on disconnect.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a ReadableStream start/cancel pair to bridge the in-process/pg event bus into an SSE response, with a heartbeat interval doubling as a presence keep-alive.

nodes.name: GET
nodes.summary: Opens an SSE stream scoped to the caller's org/user/channel topics, registers presence connect/heartbeat/disconnect, and forwards bus events as SSE frames.

nodes.name: access.test.ts
nodes.summary: Vitest unit tests for the pure chat access predicates, covering public/private/DM visibility, cross-org denial, posting, channel management, and message deletion rules.

nodes.name: access.ts
nodes.summary: Pure, testable access-control predicates for chat channels (see/post/manage/delete-message) plus loadChannelAndMembership, the single DB helper routes use to fetch a channel and the viewer's membership.

nodes.name: canSeeChannelGiven
nodes.summary: Decides channel visibility: org-scoped public channels are visible to all org members, private channels and DMs only to their members.

nodes.name: canPostToChannelGiven
nodes.summary: Decides posting rights: DMs require membership, public channels allow any org member, private channels require membership.

nodes.name: canManageChannelGiven
nodes.summary: Decides channel management rights: org OWNER/ADMIN or a channel OWNER/ADMIN member, never for DMs.

nodes.name: canDeleteMessageGiven
nodes.summary: Decides message deletion rights: the author may always delete; otherwise channel-manage rights are required.
