nodes.name: 20260526030627_phase_c_drop_legacy
nodes.summary: Phase C destructive cleanup that drops the legacy agile tables (sprints, sprint_capacities, first-generation objectives and key_results), removes projects.methodology and work_items.sprint_id/type columns, drops the Methodology and WorkItemType enums, and makes work_items.work_item_type_id required.

nodes.name: 20260527204215_add_meeting_title
nodes.summary: Adds a required title column (defaulting to empty string) to the sync_meetings table.

nodes.name: 20260528022522_add_bg_urls
nodes.summary: Adds optional bg_dark_url and bg_light_url columns to user_preferences so users can set custom background images per color theme.

nodes.name: 20260528031245_custom_field_key_unique_per_org
nodes.summary: Tightens custom field key uniqueness from (org, project, key) to (org, key), first de-duplicating existing rows by suffixing later duplicates with their short id so the new unique index can be created without data loss.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a ROW_NUMBER() window CTE to deterministically pick which duplicate rows to rename before swapping unique indexes.

nodes.name: 20260528123414_add_cli_session_id
nodes.summary: Adds an optional cli_session_id column to chat_conversations, linking assistant conversations to CLI (Foreman daemon) sessions.

nodes.name: 20260528125440_add_mcp_servers
nodes.summary: Creates the mcp_servers table storing per-organization MCP server configurations (stdio command/args/env or HTTP url/headers, transport type, enabled flag) with an org_id index.

nodes.name: mcp_servers
nodes.summary: Per-organization registry of configured MCP servers, holding transport type, launch command/args/env for stdio servers or url/headers for HTTP servers, and an enabled toggle.

nodes.name: 20260528150000_add_embeddings
nodes.summary: Adds JSONB search_vector columns to notes, work_items, contracts, and sync_meetings for RAG semantic search, storing a token-frequency bag scored in JS because the pgvector extension is unavailable.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately uses JSONB instead of pgvector(384); the comments document a planned follow-up migration to dense vectors once the vector extension is installed.

nodes.name: 20260528160000_rename_chat_to_assistant
nodes.summary: Data-preserving rename of the AI assistant tables: chat_conversations/chat_messages become assistant_conversations/assistant_messages, along with their enum, indexes, and PK/FK constraint names, freeing the chat_* namespace for team chat.
nodes.languageNotes: Renames constraints explicitly because Postgres constraint names are unique per schema and do not follow table renames automatically.

nodes.name: 20260528170000_team_chat_phase_1
nodes.summary: Phase 1 of the team chat feature: creates six tables (chat_channels, chat_channel_members, chat_messages, chat_message_reactions, chat_message_attachments, chat_message_mentions) with unique slugs and DM keys per org, read-state tracking, and threading via parent_message_id.

nodes.name: chat_channels
nodes.summary: Team chat channels per organization, supporting named channels, private channels, project-linked channels, and DMs via a unique dm_key, with archival and last-message tracking.

nodes.name: chat_channel_members
nodes.summary: Channel membership join table tracking each member's role, notification preference, mute window, and read state (last_read_message_id/last_read_at) with a unique (channel, user) constraint.

nodes.name: chat_messages
nodes.summary: Team chat messages with soft delete, edit timestamps, and threading via parent_message_id, indexed for channel timelines, thread views, and per-author history.

nodes.name: chat_message_reactions
nodes.summary: Emoji reactions on chat messages, unique per (message, user, emoji).

nodes.name: chat_message_attachments
nodes.summary: File and image attachments on chat messages, storing url or storage key, content type, size, and image dimensions along with the uploading user.

nodes.name: chat_message_mentions
nodes.summary: User @-mentions extracted from chat messages, unique per (message, user) and indexed for per-user mention feeds.

nodes.name: 20260528180000_backfill_notification_url
nodes.summary: Data-only backfill that synthesizes a url for legacy notification rows from their ref_type (work_item/objective to /projects, contact to /crm, note to /notes), allowing the notification dropdown to drop its client-side route fallback.

nodes.name: 20260529000000_chat_messages_tsvector
nodes.summary: Adds a GENERATED ALWAYS STORED tsvector column plus a GIN index to chat_messages for Postgres full-text search; the database maintains the column automatically so application code never writes it.
nodes.languageNotes: The generated column is intentionally raw-SQL-managed and not modeled in schema.prisma, which later caused reconciliation care in the chat_alerts_presence no-op migration.

nodes.name: 20260530000000_user_prefs_dnd
nodes.summary: Adds do-not-disturb columns (dnd_enabled flag plus start/end times and timezone) to user_preferences for notification quiet hours.

nodes.name: 20260531000000_chat_message_kind
nodes.summary: Creates the ChatMessageKind enum (USER, ACTION, SYSTEM, ASSISTANT) and adds a kind column to chat_messages defaulting to USER, distinguishing human messages from system and assistant output in team chat.

nodes.name: 20260531010000_chat_pinned_messages
nodes.summary: Creates the chat_pinned_messages table recording which messages are pinned in each channel, by whom and when, with a unique (channel, message) constraint.

nodes.name: chat_pinned_messages
nodes.summary: Pinned-message records per chat channel, tracking the pinning user and timestamp, unique per (channel, message) and indexed for recent-pins listings.

nodes.name: 20260602000000_add_okr_models
nodes.summary: Recreates the OKR data model (second generation, after the legacy tables were dropped in phase C): objectives scoped to org and optional project, and key_results with start/current/target values and sort ordering.

nodes.name: objectives
nodes.summary: OKR objectives scoped to an organization and optionally a project, with owner, period, status, and computed progress.

nodes.name: key_results
nodes.summary: Measurable key results attached to an objective, tracking start/current/target values with a unit, status, owner, and sort order.

nodes.name: 20260602010000_add_feedback_portal
nodes.summary: Creates the feedback portal tables: feedback_items (typed suggestions/bugs with status and denormalized vote_count) and feedback_votes with one-vote-per-user enforcement.

nodes.name: feedback_items
nodes.summary: User-submitted feedback items per organization with type, status workflow, and a denormalized vote_count, indexed by (org, status).

nodes.name: feedback_votes
nodes.summary: Upvotes on feedback items, unique per (feedback_item, user) to enforce one vote per user.

nodes.name: 20260602020000_add_expense_approval
nodes.summary: Adds an expense approval workflow: ExpenseStatus enum (DRAFT/SUBMITTED/APPROVED/REJECTED), status/approval/submission columns on expenses, an (org, status) index, and a backfill that grandfathers all pre-existing expenses as APPROVED.

nodes.name: 20260602030000_add_home_widgets
nodes.summary: Creates the home_widgets table for per-user dashboard widgets, each with a JSONB config and sort order, unique per (org, owner, type).

nodes.name: home_widgets
nodes.summary: Per-user home dashboard widget instances with a type, JSONB configuration, and sort order, allowing one widget of each type per owner per org.

nodes.name: 20260602040000_add_work_role_abac
nodes.summary: Introduces attribute-based access control: work_roles holding JSONB grants and policies per org (with built-in role support) and the org_member_work_roles assignment table with optional scoping.

nodes.name: work_roles
nodes.summary: Org-scoped work role definitions carrying JSONB grants and ABAC policies, with a unique key per org and a built-in flag for system roles.

nodes.name: org_member_work_roles
nodes.summary: Join table assigning work roles to org members with an optional scope column, keyed on (org_member, work_role).

nodes.name: 20260603120000_add_meeting_video_fields
nodes.summary: Adds video conferencing columns to sync_meetings: Google Meet space/conference identifiers, a generic meeting_url and video_provider, and a JSONB artifacts array for recordings/transcripts.

nodes.name: 20260603130000_money_float_to_decimal
nodes.summary: Converts money columns from double precision to DECIMAL(19,4) across crm_contacts, products, contracts, time_entries, revenues, and expenses; documented as requiring a coordinated deploy because the full-table rewrite is not backward-compatible.
nodes.languageNotes: The type change performs a full table rewrite under an ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock, so the file mandates applying it only in a low-traffic deploy window together with the matching code deploy.

nodes.name: 20260604000000_add_ledger_engine
nodes.summary: Creates the double-entry ledger engine: chart-of-accounts (accounts), journal_entries with per-org entry numbering, source idempotency and reversal links, journal_lines carrying debit/credit amounts with project/contract/cost allocations, and accounting_periods for period close.

nodes.name: accounts
nodes.summary: Hierarchical chart of accounts per organization with unique account codes, account type, normal balance side, and active/system flags.

nodes.name: journal_entries
nodes.summary: Ledger journal entries with per-org unique entry numbers, posting status and timestamp, a unique (source, source_id) idempotency key, and a reverses_id link for reversal entries.

nodes.name: journal_lines
nodes.summary: Debit/credit lines within a journal entry, each referencing an account and amount with optional project, contract, cost objective, and cost pool allocation dimensions.

nodes.name: accounting_periods
nodes.summary: Accounting periods per organization with start/end dates, open/closed status, and close audit fields, unique per (org, start_date).

nodes.name: 20260604030000_chat_alerts_presence
nodes.summary: Reconstructed no-op migration (SELECT 1) replacing a migration.sql lost in the v1 import; comments verify there is no real schema delta and note that the v2 cutover will squash the whole migration history into a clean 0000_init.
nodes.languageNotes: Documents pre-existing migration-history rot and explicitly protects the raw-SQL-managed content_tsv generated column from being dropped during reconciliation.

nodes.name: 20260606010000_add_tenant_class
nodes.summary: Adds a TenantClass enum (GOV/COMMERCIAL) and a NOT NULL tenant_class column on organizations with a fail-closed GOV default, backfilling existing orgs as COMMERCIAL unless their billing plan is GOV.

nodes.name: 20260606020000_add_egress_decisions
nodes.summary: Creates the egress_decisions audit table logging, per conversation turn, whether tool output values were exposed or withheld, along with a content hash, deciding component, tenant class, and applied ceiling.

nodes.name: egress_decisions
nodes.summary: Audit log of per-turn egress decisions for assistant conversations: value kind, tool name, exposed flag, withheld count, content hash, decider, tenant class, and ceiling, indexed by conversation and time.

nodes.name: add_pgvector
nodes.summary: Enables the pgvector extension and adds nullable 384-dim MiniLM embedding columns with HNSW cosine indexes to notes, work_items, contracts, and sync_meetings, powering in-boundary semantic (RAG) search.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses HNSW approximate-nearest-neighbour indexes with vector_cosine_ops for the `<=>` cosine-distance operator; legacy search_vector JSON columns are left in place but no longer written.

nodes.name: audit_immutability
nodes.summary: AU-9/AU-11 hardening for audit_logs and egress_decisions: drops org/user FK cascades so audit survives deletions, adds monotonic seq IDENTITY columns, installs append-only triggers that block UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE for all roles, and splits privileges so the cosmos_app role can never mutate audit rows.
nodes.languageNotes: Combines row-level BEFORE triggers with role-based REVOKE and ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES for defense-in-depth append-only enforcement.

nodes.name: add_sso_oidc_rp
nodes.summary: Creates the idp_connections table for per-org OIDC relying-party SSO configuration (issuer, client credentials, attribute/role mapping, JIT provisioning) and the federated_identities table linking users to IdP subjects.

nodes.name: audit_hash_chain
nodes.summary: Builds an in-DB tamper-evidence SHA-256 hash chain for audit_logs and egress_decisions: BEFORE INSERT triggers set row_hash/prev_hash on every row, an O(1) audit_chain_head pointer table tracks the chain tail under a row lock, and verify_audit_chain() detects any insert/delete/reorder/modification of history.
nodes.languageNotes: Hashes use length-framed BYTEA concatenation (no text separators) to stay safe for NUL bytes, and hash metadata as jsonb::text to avoid jsonb_each errors on non-object JSON values.

nodes.name: connector_credentials
nodes.summary: Creates the connector_credentials table storing AES-256-GCM vault-sealed OAuth secrets for external connectors, one row per (org, provider, user), replacing plaintext token storage per SC-28 protect-at-rest requirements.

nodes.name: org_level_connector_creds
nodes.summary: Extends connector_credentials to support org-level shared credentials by making user_id nullable and replacing the plain unique index with two disjoint partial unique indexes: one per (org, provider, user) for user-scoped rows and one per (org, provider) for the single NULL-user org-level row.
nodes.languageNotes: Partial unique indexes with complementary WHERE clauses work around Postgres treating NULLs as distinct in plain unique constraints.

nodes.name: egress_handles
nodes.summary: Creates the egress_handles opaque-handle resolver store (AC-4 CUI-by-reference): maps unguessable random tokens to vault-sealed CUI values scoped to a conversation, so the CUI-blind model orchestrates tokens while real values are resolved only in-boundary; rows are short-lived and swept by a TTL cleanup job.

nodes.name: add_frozen_orgs
nodes.summary: Creates the frozen_orgs operational flag table used during per-tenant cutover: a row marks an org as write-frozen so the request proxy returns HTTP 405 on mutating verbs while its data is migrated, keyed by both org_id and org_slug and deliberately not FK'd to organizations.

nodes.name: mcp_seal_env_headers
nodes.summary: Seals MCP server secrets at rest: adds env_enc and headers_enc TEXT columns holding AES-256-GCM vault envelopes and drops the plaintext env/headers JSON columns from mcp_servers (safe because MCP execution was dormant with no data to migrate).

nodes.name: drop_google_refresh_token
nodes.summary: Drops the legacy plaintext users.google_refresh_token column now that the sealed connector_credentials store is the sole source of truth for Google OAuth refresh tokens; a drain script must sweep remaining tokens to the sealed store before this runs on a non-empty instance.

nodes.name: audit_retention_checkpoint
nodes.summary: AU-11 retention-purge support for the audit hash chain: adds the HMAC-signed audit_chain_checkpoint table recording the seq and row_hash at each purge boundary, and replaces verify_audit_chain() with a checkpoint-aware version that anchors verification at either genesis or the latest checkpoint so sanctioned purges of the oldest rows do not break tamper-evidence.

nodes.name: data_classification_project_fk
nodes.summary: Cutover-baseline reconciliation adding the missing data_classifications.project_id foreign key onto projects (ON DELETE CASCADE), making the v2 schema structurally identical to the reconciled prod baseline checked by the schema-parity gate; guarded in a DO block for idempotency.

nodes.name: add_org_runtime_config
nodes.summary: Creates the org_runtime_config table holding one row of per-org runtime feature switches: connector allowlist enablement, the set of enabled connectors, breadth-mode, and MCP enablement.

nodes.name: idp_connections
nodes.summary: Per-org identity-provider connection: OIDC issuer URL, client ID, encrypted client secret, scopes, attribute and role mapping, JIT provisioning settings, and enabled/enforced flags; unique per org.

nodes.name: federated_identities
nodes.summary: Links a local user to an IdP connection and subject identifier, unique per (idp_conn_id, subject), so SSO logins resolve to existing accounts.

nodes.name: audit_chain_head
nodes.summary: One-row-per-audited-table mutable state cache of the current hash-chain tail (head_hash); read and advanced in O(1) under SELECT FOR UPDATE by the insert trigger so chain extension is serialized without table scans. Deliberately not an audit table; tampering here is still detected by verify_audit_chain().

nodes.name: connector_credentials
nodes.summary: Sealed credential store: vault-envelope secret_enc plus provider metadata, keyed by org, provider, and (optionally, after slice 2) user; the sole at-rest location for connector OAuth secrets.

nodes.name: egress_handles
nodes.summary: Conversation-scoped mapping of unique random tokens to AES-sealed CUI values (value_enc) with entity/field metadata; short-lived rows indexed by token, conversation, and created_at for TTL sweeps.

nodes.name: frozen_orgs
nodes.summary: Write-freeze registry for cutover windows: org id/slug, freeze reason, who froze it and when; matched by the request proxy on both slug and UUID URL forms.

nodes.name: audit_chain_checkpoint
nodes.summary: HMAC-signed record of each audit retention purge: the max purged seq and the row_hash at that seq per audited table; the latest checkpoint per table is the verification anchor after a purge. App role is SELECT-only — only the owner inserts during a purge.

nodes.name: org_runtime_config
nodes.summary: Singleton-per-org runtime switches: allowlist_enabled, enabled_connectors, breadth_enabled, and mcp_enabled, unique on org_id.

nodes.name: add_agent_policy
nodes.summary: Creates the agent_policy table holding one row of per-org agent guardrails: allowed/denied tool lists, denied domains, a max result limit, and an optional allowed-project-id scope for the autonomous agent runtime.

nodes.name: prod_parity_reconciliation
nodes.summary: Large cutover-parity migration creating 18 tables the live prod DB has but v2 lacked, spanning finance (invoices, invoice_line_items, payments, employees, pay_runs, tax_rates, bank_accounts, bank_transactions, bank_rules), chat (thread followers, alert keywords, bots, bot channels, bot runs), documents, work-item links/attachments, and org AI settings, with their unique keys and indexes.

nodes.name: column_parity
nodes.summary: Column-level cutover reconciliation adding prod-only columns to shared tables — work_items import-provenance fields (external_source/id/key, source_record, estimates), org_security_settings session/MFA policy columns, boards.slug, chat_channel_members.pinned, users presence fields, and time_entries.pay_run_id — matching prod's exact shape for a zero-loss tenant copy.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately omits prod columns v2 replaced (plaintext google_refresh_token, mcp env/headers, tsvector search columns), documenting each intentional deviation inline.

nodes.name: add_goals_milestones_kpis
nodes.summary: Adds the project-planning trio: goals (with progress tracking and links to work items/objectives), milestones (with due dates and work-item links), and KPIs (with targets, direction, and time-series kpi_data_points), all org- and project-scoped.

nodes.name: journalsource_finance_values
nodes.summary: Additively extends the JournalSource enum with INVOICE, PAYMENT, and PAYROLL values so finance-module postings can be attributed to their originating documents.

nodes.name: add_local_auth_mfa
nodes.summary: Adds local username/password and TOTP MFA columns to users: password_hash, password_set_at, mfa_enabled, mfa_secret, mfa_recovery_codes, and mfa_enrolled_at, all nullable or defaulted so the change is additive.

nodes.name: add_auth_provider_configs
nodes.summary: Creates the auth_provider_configs table storing per-provider authentication configuration with an encrypted secret (secret_enc), an enabled flag, and audit fields, unique per provider.

nodes.name: invitation_work_roles
nodes.summary: Adds a work_role_ids TEXT[] column to invitations so granular RBAC/ABAC work roles can be pre-assigned at invite time and applied on acceptance.

nodes.name: session_last_activity
nodes.summary: Adds a last_activity_at timestamp to sessions as the sliding-window idle-timeout anchor, defaulting existing rows to now() so the deploy does not log everyone out.

nodes.name: add_user_ai_settings
nodes.summary: Creates the user_ai_settings table holding one row per user of AI-provider preferences and OAuth tokens (access/refresh tokens with expiry), unique on user_id.

nodes.name: feedback_attachments_telemetry
nodes.summary: Creates the feedback_attachments table for files attached to feedback-portal items (kind, URL or storage key, content type, size, uploader), indexed by feedback item and by uploader/created_at for telemetry queries.

nodes.name: meeting_type_options
nodes.summary: Creates the meeting_type_options table of per-org configurable meeting-type labels with sort order, unique per (org, label).

nodes.name: agent_policy
nodes.summary: Singleton-per-org agent guardrail policy: allowed/denied tool sets, denied domains, max result limit, and optional allowed-project scoping; unique on org_id.

nodes.name: org_ai_settings
nodes.summary: Per-org AI provider configuration: provider/model choice plus Anthropic, Claude OAuth, and OpenAI credential columns with OAuth token lifecycle fields; unique on org_id.

nodes.name: work_item_links
nodes.summary: Typed directed links between work items (source/target item ids with a link type), org-scoped and indexed by source item.

nodes.name: work_item_attachments
nodes.summary: File attachments on work items: file name, URL, MIME type, size, and optional external reference, indexed by org and work item.

nodes.name: invoices
nodes.summary: Org-scoped customer invoices with number (unique per org), contact/contract references, bill-to details, status, dates, currency, and subtotal/tax/total/amount-paid money fields.

nodes.name: invoice_line_items
nodes.summary: Line items belonging to an invoice: description, quantity, unit price, tax rate, computed amount, optional product reference, and sort order.

nodes.name: payments
nodes.summary: Payments received against invoices: amount, method, reference, and received-at timestamp, indexed by org and invoice.

nodes.name: employees
nodes.summary: Org employee records linked to users (unique per org+user) with employment type, cost rate, labor category, classification, status, and start/end dates for payroll and costing.

nodes.name: pay_runs
nodes.summary: Payroll runs per org: labeled pay periods with status, aggregate labor cost, and posted-at timestamp.

nodes.name: tax_rates
nodes.summary: Configurable org tax rates with jurisdiction, default and active flags, used by invoicing.

nodes.name: documents
nodes.summary: Org/project-scoped uploaded documents with title, classification level, storage key, filename, content type, size, and uploader; indexed by org and project.

nodes.name: chat_thread_followers
nodes.summary: Tracks which users follow a chat thread (channel + parent message) with last-read timestamps, unique per user and parent message.

nodes.name: chat_alert_keywords
nodes.summary: Per-user chat alert keywords (unique per user+keyword) that trigger mention-style notifications when matched in messages.

nodes.name: chat_bots
nodes.summary: Org chat bots with a unique key per org, display name, persona, model, tool scope, enabled MCP set, optional cron schedule, and a backing bot user account.

nodes.name: chat_bot_channels
nodes.summary: Bot-to-channel enrollments (unique per bot+channel) with auto-respond and enabled flags.

nodes.name: chat_bot_runs
nodes.summary: Execution log of chat bot runs: triggering message and user, run status, and timestamps, indexed by bot and created_at.

nodes.name: bank_accounts
nodes.summary: Org bank accounts with institution, masked number, currency, provider, and an optional ledger account link for reconciliation.

nodes.name: bank_transactions
nodes.summary: Imported bank transactions deduplicated by external_id and fingerprint per account, with posted date, amount, pending/status flags, category, and matched expense/revenue references for reconciliation.

nodes.name: bank_rules
nodes.summary: Prioritized auto-categorization rules for bank transactions matching on description substring, direction, and amount range.

nodes.name: goals
nodes.summary: Org/project-scoped goals with status, numeric progress and progress mode, target date, owner, and sort order.

nodes.name: goal_links
nodes.summary: Polymorphic links from a goal to either a work item or an OKR objective, discriminated by a kind column.

nodes.name: milestones
nodes.summary: Org/project-scoped milestones with due date, manual or auto status, completion timestamp, owner, and sort order.

nodes.name: milestone_links
nodes.summary: Join table associating milestones with the work items that roll up into them.

nodes.name: kpis
nodes.summary: Org/project-scoped KPIs with unit, target and current values, and an improvement direction, ordered for display.

nodes.name: kpi_data_points
nodes.summary: Time-series measurements for a KPI: value, recorded-at timestamp, and optional note, indexed by KPI and recorded_at.

nodes.name: auth_provider_configs
nodes.summary: One row per auth provider: enabled flag, encrypted provider secret (secret_enc), and updated-by audit field, unique on provider.

nodes.name: user_ai_settings
nodes.summary: Per-user AI provider choice and OAuth token set (access/refresh tokens with expiry), unique on user_id.

nodes.name: feedback_attachments
nodes.summary: Attachments on feedback items: kind, URL or storage key, filename, content type, size, and uploader, indexed by feedback item and by uploader/created_at.

nodes.name: meeting_type_options
nodes.summary: Per-org meeting-type label options with sort order, unique per (org, label).

nodes.name: 20260611080000_meeting_type_options_org_fk
nodes.summary: Repair migration adding the missing org_id foreign key (ON DELETE CASCADE) to meeting_type_options so deleting an organization no longer leaves orphaned meeting-type rows. Guarded by a NOT-EXISTS check on pg_constraint, making it idempotent.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses a PL/pgSQL DO block with a pg_constraint existence check to make constraint addition re-runnable, since ADD CONSTRAINT has no IF NOT EXISTS form.

nodes.name: 20260611090000_crm_contact_fields
nodes.summary: Adds first-class email, phone, company, and title columns to crm_contacts that the contact edit form and client type already used but which previously had no backing columns, so edits were silently dropped. Additive, nullable, and idempotent via IF NOT EXISTS.

nodes.name: 20260611100000_crm_owner_id_to_user_id
nodes.summary: Data backfill converting crm_contacts.owner_id from OrgMember membership-record ids to User ids so the ABAC engine's owns_resource rule matches the real owner for CRM_UPDATE/CRM_DELETE grants. Only rewrites rows still matching an org_members.id, making the update idempotent.

nodes.name: 20260612120000_add_roadmap_nodes
nodes.summary: Creates the roadmap_nodes table storing hierarchical, org- and project-scoped roadmap content (kind, section, category, title, body, anchor, JSON meta, self-referencing parent_id) with unique keys on external_ref and anchor plus lookup indexes.

nodes.name: roadmap_nodes
nodes.summary: Org/project-scoped roadmap content tree: each node has a kind, section, category, title, body, stable anchor, JSON meta, sort_order, and an optional parent_id enabling nested roadmap structure.

nodes.name: 20260613000000_add_documents
nodes.summary: File-ingestion migration extending the existing CUI-aware documents table with format, parse status (DocumentStatus enum), parse_error, and page_count, and creating the document_blocks table holding each document's parsed, ordered block tree.
nodes.languageNotes: Hand-authored rather than generated by prisma migrate diff; relies on DB-init default privileges instead of explicit GRANTs for the cosmos_app role.

nodes.name: document_blocks
nodes.summary: Normalized block tree for parsed documents: typed blocks (heading, paragraph, list, table, code, image, quote, page break) with text/html/JSON payloads, per-document unique anchors, ordinal ordering, and a self-referencing parent for nesting. Cascades on document deletion.

nodes.name: 20260613010000_add_document_item_links
nodes.summary: Creates the document_item_links join table connecting parsed document blocks to arbitrary work items via polymorphic item_type/item_id pairs, indexed for lookup by item and by block.

nodes.name: document_item_links
nodes.summary: Polymorphic link table tying a document block to a project item (item_type + item_id), scoped by org and project, enabling traceability between ingested documents and work items.

nodes.name: 20260613020000_api_key_created_by
nodes.summary: Adds creator attribution to API keys: a created_by_id column on api_keys with a supporting index so keys can be traced back to the user who issued them.

nodes.name: 20260613030000_api_key_prefix_unique
nodes.summary: Adds a unique index on api_keys (org_id, prefix) so API key prefixes are unambiguous within an organization, enabling safe prefix-based key lookup.

nodes.name: 20260615000000_classification_fouo_to_cui
nodes.summary: Data migration retiring the FOUO classification marking in favor of CUI per DoDI 5200.48, rewriting legacy rows in data_classifications and documents. The FOUO enum value is retained for back-compat with the egress marking detector; the update is idempotent.

nodes.name: 20260616000000_add_org_entitlements
nodes.summary: Creates the org_entitlements table controlling per-organization feature gating: allowlist toggles and arrays for enabled modules and sectors, keyed one-to-one to an organization.

nodes.name: org_entitlements
nodes.summary: One-row-per-org entitlement record with module_allowlist_enabled/enabled_modules and sector_allowlist_enabled/enabled_sectors, gating which platform modules and sectors an organization can use.

nodes.name: 20260619000000_add_user_skin
nodes.summary: One-line migration adding a nullable skin_id column to user_preferences so each user can select a UI skin preset.

nodes.name: 20260620000000_add_org_brand
nodes.summary: White-label branding migration adding five nullable columns to organizations (default_skin_id, brand_name, agent_name, tagline, wake_word). NULL means inherit the deployment brand, so existing orgs are unaffected until an admin overrides a field; idempotent via IF NOT EXISTS.
nodes.languageNotes: default_skin_id is validated against SKIN_PRESETS at the API boundary rather than by a DB constraint, so new skin presets never require a migration.

nodes.name: 20260627000000_add_govcon_pm_models
nodes.summary: Foundational GovCon program-management migration creating four org/project-scoped tracker tables — risks, deliverables, blockers, and change_requests — each with per-org unique codes, status indexes, classification markings, and escalation flags.

nodes.name: risks
nodes.summary: Program risk register: coded risks with likelihood/impact/score, level, owner, mitigation, status, trend, escalation flag, target date, and classification marking, scoped by org and project.

nodes.name: deliverables
nodes.summary: Contract deliverables tracker: coded deliverables tied to a CLIN with baseline due date, actual submission, government acceptance, revision cycle count, owner, escalation flag, and classification.

nodes.name: blockers
nodes.summary: Program blockers log: typed blockers with status, what-unblocks description, owner, customer-notification flag, identified/resolved timestamps, escalation flag, and classification.

nodes.name: change_requests
nodes.summary: Contract change-request tracker: typed change requests with status, cost and schedule-days impact, mod-required flag, decision timestamp, and classification marking.

nodes.name: 20260627010000_add_program_branch
nodes.summary: Creates the program_branches lookup table of org-scoped branch codes and names with sort ordering and a per-org unique code, used to attribute GovCon tracker items to organizational branches.

nodes.name: program_branches
nodes.summary: Org-scoped reference table of program branches (code, name, sort_order) with a unique code per organization.

nodes.name: 20260627020000_risk_field_parity
nodes.summary: Brings the risks table to field parity with the source tracker by adding MONITORING, MITIGATED, and ESCALATED values to the RiskStatus enum plus contingency and date_identified columns.

nodes.name: 20260627030000_p1_2_tracker_parity
nodes.summary: Large tracker-parity migration expanding the DeliverableStatus, BlockerType, BlockerStatus, and ChangeRequestStatus enums, adding schedule-recovery fields to milestones and detail fields to deliverables, blockers, and change_requests, and creating the deliverable_revisions table to track government review cycles.

nodes.name: deliverable_revisions
nodes.summary: Per-deliverable revision-cycle history: each row records a review cycle with date returned, comment summary, owner, revised and actual dates, days to resolve, and government acceptance.

nodes.name: 20260627040000_initiated_by_snake_case
nodes.summary: One-line rename of change_requests.initiatedBy to initiated_by, fixing a camelCase column introduced by the tracker-parity migration to match the schema's snake_case convention.

nodes.name: 20260628000000_kpi_auto_source
nodes.summary: Adds automated KPI sourcing: a KpiAutoSource enum (MANUAL, VELOCITY, COMPLETION_PCT, THROUGHPUT, OPEN_ITEMS, AVG_CYCLE_TIME) plus auto_source and auto_window_days columns on kpis so KPI values can be computed from project activity instead of entered manually.

nodes.name: 20260629000000_vendor_govcon
nodes.summary: GovCon vendor enrichment: adds cage_code, perf_rating, and socio_economic columns to partners, plus a project_id column and (org_id, project_id) index on contracts to scope contracts to projects.

nodes.name: 20260629010000_project_member_allocation
nodes.summary: Adds an allocation_percent column to project_members so staffing allocation per project member can be tracked.

nodes.name: 20260629020000_clin_burn
nodes.summary: Creates the clins table modeling contract line items (code, title, total and funded value, period of performance, status) per org and project, with a lookup index and a per-project unique code, supporting CLIN burn tracking.

nodes.name: clins
nodes.summary: Contract line item (CLIN) record with monetary value, funded_value, period-of-performance dates, and status, unique by code within an org/project.

nodes.name: 20260629030000_gap_fields_1
nodes.summary: Gap-filling migration adding NDA and point-of-contact fields to partners, agreement/funding/invoicing fields to contracts, and notes plus reference fields to milestones, deliverables, blockers, and change_requests.

nodes.name: 20260629040000_staffing_compliance
nodes.summary: Adds staffing-compliance tracking columns to project_members: access, CAC, NDA, and training statuses, CAC expiry, on_contract flag, and compliance notes for GovCon workforce compliance.

nodes.name: 20260629050000_polymorphic_comments_activity
nodes.summary: Generalizes activities and comments beyond work items by adding polymorphic subject_type/subject_id columns, relaxing work_item_id to nullable, and indexing (org_id, subject_type, subject_id) for subject-scoped lookups.

nodes.name: 20260629060000_pm_links
nodes.summary: Creates the pm_links table for typed, directional links between arbitrary program-management items (from_type/from_id to to_type/to_id) with creator attribution, indexed both directions and unique per link pair.

nodes.name: pm_links
nodes.summary: Polymorphic cross-item link record connecting any two PM entities via from/to type-id pairs, scoped by org and project, with a uniqueness constraint preventing duplicate links.

nodes.name: 20260630120000_user_tab_prefs
nodes.summary: Additive migration adding a tab_prefs JSONB column to user_preferences, storing per-user, per-project tab layout preferences (order, hidden tabs, labels, default tab) keyed by projectId.

nodes.name: 20260701000000_entity_references
nodes.summary: Creates the entity_references table, an org-scoped generic cross-entity link table (source type/id to target type/id) with a uniqueness constraint on the source-target pair and lookup indexes in both directions.

nodes.name: 20260703000000_backfill_board_slugs
nodes.summary: Data-only backfill that generates human-readable slugs for boards created before slugs existed, mirroring the app's slugify rules (lowercase, hyphenated, capped at 50 chars) and deduplicating per project with -2, -3 suffixes via a window function.
nodes.languageNotes: Uses chained CTEs with regexp_replace and row_number() OVER (PARTITION BY project_id, base) to slugify and dedupe entirely in SQL.

nodes.name: 20260703120000_add_kr_checkins
nodes.summary: Creates the key_result_checkins table recording OKR check-in history per key result — value, confidence, RAG status, note, and blockers — indexed by key result and creation time.

nodes.name: 20260703140000_objective_alignment
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable self-referencing parent_objective_id foreign key to objectives so an objective can ladder up to a parent objective, with SET NULL on parent delete and a supporting index.

nodes.name: 20260703160000_kr_lower_is_better
nodes.summary: Adds a lower_is_better boolean to key_results for metrics that improve as they decrease (latency, cost, defects), so progress measures start-to-target descending.

nodes.name: 20260703170000_objective_sort_order
nodes.summary: Adds a sort_order integer to objectives for drag-to-reorder on the Objectives tab, then backfills it per project from creation order so existing lists keep their ordering.

nodes.name: 20260706070000_add_work_item_assignees
nodes.summary: Creates the work_item_assignees junction table enabling multiple ordered assignees per work item, with a uniqueness constraint on (work_item_id, user_id) and a user lookup index.

nodes.name: 20260706130000_add_feedback_remediation
nodes.summary: Adds nullable delivered_at, work_item_id, and triage JSONB columns to feedback_items for the auto-remediation loop that delivers open feedback into the work backlog, plus an index backing the poller's open-and-undelivered scan.

nodes.name: 20260706150000_add_work_item_watchers
nodes.summary: Creates the org-scoped work_item_watchers junction table so users can subscribe to work item updates, unique per (work_item_id, user_id) with an org/user lookup index.

nodes.name: 20260706170000_add_saved_views
nodes.summary: Creates the saved_views table storing per-owner named JSON filter definitions with a shared flag, unique per (owner_id, name) and indexed by org.

nodes.name: 20260707053924_add_program_increments
nodes.summary: Introduces the SAFe Program Increment hierarchy by adding a PROGRAM_INCREMENT value to the CycleKind enum and a self-referential parent_id on cycles so a PI cycle can contain sprint cycles.

nodes.name: 20260707105344_add_key_result_links
nodes.summary: Creates the key_result_links join table connecting OKR key results to work items, unique per (key_result_id, work_item_id) with org and work item indexes.

nodes.name: 20260707120651_add_gantt_baseline_work_category
nodes.summary: Gantt enhancements: creates the WorkCategory enum (BUSINESS, ENABLER) and adds frozen baseline_start/baseline_end dates plus a work_category column to work_items for slippage tracking and SAFe work classification.

nodes.name: 20260708154434_feedback_project
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable project_id foreign key to feedback_items for multi-project feedback routing, with SET NULL on project delete so deleting a project never cascade-deletes feedback.

nodes.name: 20260708171425_normalize_unscoped_automation
nodes.summary: Data-only fix that flips autonomousDelivery.enabled to false inside organizations.settings JSON for configs with no projectIds, preventing the new enable-gate from trapping the settings form on never-actionable configs.
nodes.languageNotes: Mutates nested JSONB in place with jsonb_set and guards on jsonb_typeof/jsonb_array_length rather than altering any schema.

nodes.name: 20260710160000_backfill_feedback_status_from_work_items
nodes.summary: Data-only backfill that updates stale PLANNED feedback_items to DONE or IN_PROGRESS by pattern-matching their linked work item's column_key, mirroring the app's feedbackStatusForColumn logic; OPEN, DONE, and DECLINED rows are never touched.

nodes.name: 20260711010000_add_voice_close_word
nodes.summary: Adds a nullable voice_close_word text column to user_preferences — the per-user spoken word that ends and sends a dictated assistant message (defaults to 'send it' when NULL).

nodes.name: 20260711130000_add_in_review_feedback_status
nodes.summary: Adds an IN_REVIEW value to the FeedbackStatus enum to distinguish work parked in human review (a built draft PR awaiting approval) from actively in-progress work.

nodes.name: 20260711220000_add_foreman_observability
nodes.summary: Adds observability for the Foreman delivery daemon: a foreman_state singleton heartbeat table (pid, worker slots, queue depth, breaker state) and a foreman_events log table for per-ticket events with severity and payload.

nodes.name: 20260712010000_mask_columns_to_text
nodes.summary: Converts the permission bitfield columns org_members.permissions and work_roles.grants from BIGINT to decimal-string TEXT because masks with bits >= 63 overflow BIGINT; the USING ::text cast is a safe no-op where a column already drifted to text.

nodes.name: 20260713150000_add_foreman_ai_settings
nodes.summary: Creates the foreman_ai_settings table storing one AI provider configuration per organization — provider name plus OAuth access/refresh tokens and expiry — for the Foreman daemon's AI integration.

nodes.name: 20260713170000_simplify_plan_tiers
nodes.summary: Recreates the billing Plan enum from FREE/TEAM/BUSINESS/ENTERPRISE/GOV down to BASIC/TEAM/ENTERPRISE by renaming the old type, casting organizations.plan through a CASE remap, then backfilling every org to ENTERPRISE while feature-gating is deferred.
nodes.languageNotes: Postgres cannot drop enum values, so the migration uses the rename-old-type, create-new-type, USING-cast, drop-old-type pattern.

nodes.name: 20260713180000_email_password_invite
nodes.summary: Additive onboarding migration for email/password invites: adds must_change_password and mfa_required flags to users, and sign_in_method plus mfa_required to invitations, preserving the existing OAuth invite flow.

nodes.name: 20260714120000_add_org_email_settings
nodes.summary: Creates the org_email_settings table holding one outbound email configuration per organization — provider, API key, from address, and enabled flag — unique per org_id.

nodes.name: entity_references
nodes.summary: Org-scoped polymorphic link table connecting any source entity (type + id) to any target entity, with creator attribution and a unique source-target pair constraint.

nodes.name: key_result_checkins
nodes.summary: Append-only check-in history for OKR key results capturing value, confidence, RAG status, note, blockers, and who checked in.

nodes.name: work_item_assignees
nodes.summary: Junction table mapping work items to multiple ordered assignees, unique per (work_item_id, user_id).

nodes.name: work_item_watchers
nodes.summary: Org-scoped junction table recording which users watch a work item for update notifications, unique per (work_item_id, user_id).

nodes.name: saved_views
nodes.summary: Per-owner named saved view storing a JSON filter definition with an optional shared flag, unique per (owner_id, name).

nodes.name: key_result_links
nodes.summary: Join table linking OKR key results to the work items that deliver them, unique per (key_result_id, work_item_id).

nodes.name: foreman_state
nodes.summary: Singleton heartbeat table for the Foreman delivery daemon tracking pid, daemon version, worker slots, queue depth, in-flight work, circuit breaker state, and stop-file detection.

nodes.name: foreman_events
nodes.summary: Event log for the Foreman daemon recording timestamped per-org, per-ticket events with kind, severity, message, and a JSON data payload, indexed by org and time.

nodes.name: foreman_ai_settings
nodes.summary: Per-organization AI provider configuration for the Foreman daemon holding provider name and OAuth access/refresh tokens with expiry, unique per org_id.

nodes.name: org_email_settings
nodes.summary: Per-organization outbound email configuration storing provider, API key, from address, and an enabled flag, unique per org_id.

nodes.name: 20260715120000_add_user_deactivated_at
nodes.summary: Migration adding a nullable users.deactivated_at timestamp to support account deletion as in-place anonymization plus access revocation, since RESTRICT foreign keys and FK-less authored-content columns make a hard row delete unsafe.
nodes.languageNotes: The migration comment documents why anonymization is preferred over DELETE: chat_bot_runs.triggered_by_user_id is ON DELETE RESTRICT and many created_by columns carry no foreign key.

nodes.name: 20260719155142_foreman_supervisor_settings
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder migration for the Foreman supervisor settings change; the actual DDL landed in the 20260719155211 migration of the same name.

nodes.name: 20260719155154_foreman_supervisor_settings
nodes.summary: Empty placeholder migration for the Foreman supervisor settings change; the actual DDL landed in the 20260719155211 migration of the same name.

nodes.name: 20260719155211_foreman_supervisor_settings
nodes.summary: Migration creating the per-org foreman_supervisor_settings table (mode, deliver_close/requeue/dedup/escalate toggles, confidence threshold, per-pass cap) with a unique org_id index for the Foreman delivery daemon's supervisor configuration.

nodes.name: foreman_supervisor_settings
nodes.summary: One-row-per-org table storing Foreman supervisor behavior: operating mode, deliver-close/requeue/dedup/escalate flags, confidence_threshold, and per_pass_cap, with audit columns and a unique org_id constraint.

nodes.name: 20260720152808_foreman_harness
nodes.summary: Migration creating the Foreman agent-harness tables: per-org foreman_skills (reusable skill bodies), foreman_mcp_servers (MCP server endpoints with headers), and foreman_harness_settings (enable flag plus system-prompt append), each with org-scoped unique indexes.

nodes.name: foreman_skills
nodes.summary: Per-org catalog of named Foreman skills with description, body text, enabled flag, and source, uniquely keyed on (org_id, name).

nodes.name: foreman_mcp_servers
nodes.summary: Per-org registry of MCP server endpoints for the Foreman harness, storing name, URL, request headers, and enabled flag, uniquely keyed on (org_id, name).

nodes.name: foreman_harness_settings
nodes.summary: One-row-per-org toggle table for the Foreman harness with an enabled flag and an optional system_prompt_append override, unique on org_id.

nodes.name: 20260720211711_foreman_loop_graph
nodes.summary: Migration creating the Foreman loop-graph persistence layer: foreman_loop_transition (per-iteration phase transitions with token/cost telemetry and state snapshots), foreman_loop_state (current status/phase per loop), and foreman_loop_settings (per-org wall-clock, cost-ceiling, and stall-round limits), plus supporting indexes.

nodes.name: foreman_loop_transition
nodes.summary: Append-only log of Foreman loop iterations recording from/to phase, action, termination signal, invariant results, duration, token in/out counts, cost in USD, and a state snapshot, unique on (loop_id, iteration).

nodes.name: foreman_loop_state
nodes.summary: Current-state row per Foreman loop holding status, phase, iteration counter, schema_version, and a JSON state blob, unique on loop_id and indexed by (org_id, status).

nodes.name: foreman_loop_settings
nodes.summary: Per-org Foreman loop guardrail settings: mode, wall-clock minutes, cost USD ceiling, and stall-round limit, unique on org_id.

nodes.name: 20260722120000_add_work_item_actual_start
nodes.summary: Migration adding the nullable work_items.actual_start column for the unified item date model, with a best-effort backfill from column_entered_at for items already past the not-started board columns.

nodes.name: 20260722130000_drop_retired_schedule_baselines
nodes.summary: Migration dropping the retired manual-baseline columns (work_items.baseline_start/baseline_end, milestones.baseline_date/projected_date) now that schedule health derives from actual vs. projected end dates.

nodes.name: 20260724000000_rename_cycle_to_interval
nodes.summary: Non-destructive domain rename of "cycle" to "interval" (sprint/phase/PI/release container): renames the CycleKind enum, the cycles and cycle_capacities tables, related columns, indexes, and foreign-key constraints to match Prisma naming conventions.

nodes.name: audit-worm-export.mjs
nodes.summary: AU-9 offsite immutable audit anchor: incrementally exports audit_logs and egress_decisions rows (each table its own seq watermark and object-key prefix) to NDJSON, sha256-hashes the dump, HMAC-signs a manifest, and PUTs both to an object-locked WORM S3 bucket so live-DB tampering is detectable by diff.
nodes.languageNotes: The high-water mark is derived from manifest keys, not dump keys, and dump PUTs use IfNoneMatch with tolerated 412s — making the export idempotent and gap-free under partial failure.

nodes.name: lastAttestedToSeq
nodes.summary: Lists the table's manifest objects in the WORM bucket and parses the highest attested toSeq from manifest key names, establishing the export watermark from signed manifests rather than dumps.

nodes.name: exportTable
nodes.summary: Exports one table's window: derives fromSeq from the last attested manifest, fetches rows with seq greater than it, builds a deterministic NDJSON dump, computes sha256 and an HMAC-signed manifest, and PUTs the dump then the manifest immutably.

nodes.name: putImmutable
nodes.summary: PUTs an object with IfNoneMatch so it never overwrites, treating a 412 PreconditionFailed as success (identical immutable bytes already present) and exiting hard on any other error.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Connects to Postgres, runs exportTable for audit_logs and egress_decisions as independent watermark domains, prints per-table summaries, and ensures the client is closed on both success and failure paths.

nodes.name: check-control-coverage.mjs
nodes.summary: CI gate that validates the living SSP control-coverage matrix (compliance/ssp/control-coverage.csv): requires at least 110 rows, mandatory columns per row, and an existing evidencePath for implemented non-policy controls, while exempting planned/partial/policy/inherited rows.

nodes.name: parseCsv
nodes.summary: Minimal CSV parser handling quoted cells and escaped quotes, returning header names and row objects for the control-coverage matrix.

nodes.name: check-examples.mjs

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses and validates the --in/--out/--table CLI flags, exiting with usage errors on missing arguments and rejecting table names that are not valid SQL identifiers.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Probes the proxy freeze decision for POST and GET on the org's API and slug paths while frozen, then calls unfreezeOrg and confirms a subsequent POST passes.

nodes.languageNotes: Uses stable hard-coded UUIDs so downstream acceptance assertions can target specific rows deterministically.

nodes.languageNotes: Exists so model-graph.ts can shell out once via execFileSync and keep its dmmfModels() accessor synchronous despite getDMMF being async/wasm-backed.

nodes.name: purge-audit.checkpoint-sig.test.mjs
nodes.summary: Unit test verifying that purge-audit.mjs's signCheckpoint produces the exact canonical HMAC-SHA256 signature (tableName + seq + rowHash hex) that verify-audit-chain.mjs recomputes, keeping the two scripts cryptographically in lockstep.

nodes.name: purge-audit.mjs
nodes.summary: AU-11 sanctioned audit retention-purge: the one legitimate path that deletes old audit_logs/egress_decisions rows without breaking the AU-9 hash-chain, by first recording a signed HMAC chain-checkpoint at the purge boundary inside a single owner-role transaction.
nodes.languageNotes: Guards include a WORM-ordering check against the offsite S3 manifest high-water mark and a 3-year (1095-day) NIST 800-171 retention floor with a loud test-only override env.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses CLI flags (--table, --retention-days, --hmac-key-env, --worm-toseq) into a validated options object, failing fast on unknown or missing values.

nodes.name: signCheckpoint
nodes.summary: Computes the checkpoint signature HMAC_sha256(key, tableName + seq + rowHashHex) — the canonical input verify-audit-chain.mjs recomputes to detect forged checkpoints.

nodes.name: latestWormToSeq
nodes.summary: Reads the cosmos-audit-worm S3 bucket's signed manifest keys to find the latest WORM-attested toSeq for a table, the high-water mark the purge must never exceed.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Orchestrates the purge: validates args and guards (WORM ordering, gov retention floor), then in one owner transaction sets session_replication_role=replica, inserts the signed checkpoint, and deletes rows with seq <= N; idempotent no-op when already checkpointed.

nodes.name: verify-audit-chain.mjs
nodes.summary: AU-9 tamper-evidence gate: invokes the in-DB verify_audit_chain() function on both append-only audit tables, additionally recomputes the latest checkpoint's HMAC signature (which SQL cannot do), and exits non-zero on any chain break or forged checkpoint so CI/ops can alarm.
nodes.languageNotes: Deliberately least-privilege: connects as the non-owner cosmos_app role since verification is SELECT-only; uses timingSafeEqual for signature comparison.

nodes.name: parseArgs
nodes.summary: Parses the optional --hmac-key-env CLI flag and rejects unknown arguments with a non-zero exit.

nodes.name: main
nodes.summary: Runs verify_audit_chain() per table, verifies each latest checkpoint's HMAC with timing-safe comparison, prints a human line per table to stderr plus a machine-readable JSON summary to stdout, and exits 0/1/2 for intact/error/broken.

nodes.name: generate-brand-icons.mjs

nodes.name: capacityUnitForSector
nodes.summary: Maps a project sector to its planning capacity unit: story points for software/agile projects, hours for everything else.

nodes.name: unitAbbrev
nodes.summary: Returns the short abbreviation for a capacity unit (e.g. 'pts' or 'h') for compact UI display.

nodes.name: unitNoun

nodes.name: suggestMemberCapacity

nodes.name: itemSize

nodes.name: isOverCommitted

tour.title: Project Overview
tour.description: Start with README.md to understand what Cosmos is: a multi-tenant project- and program-management platform (boards, OKRs, RAID logs, SAFe program increments) with a distinctive feedback-to-delivery automation pipeline, where user feedback is auto-triaged into backlogs and an autonomous 'Foreman' daemon can ship the work. AGENTS.md complements this with the contributor conventions that govern the codebase — SemVer rules, secret hygiene, and coding norms. Together they give you the vocabulary for everything that follows.

tour.title: Application Entry Point
tour.description: Cosmos is a Next.js 16 App Router application, so the root layout is where every page begins: it generates brand-driven metadata, inlines skin CSS presets, and mounts global providers for branding, motion, and telemetry. Because Next.js routes by filesystem convention rather than imports, this file is deliberately thin — the real composition happens in the nested layouts you will see in Step 7. Note the multi-product 'brand' concept here: one codebase serves multiple branded deployments.
tour.languageLesson: In the Next.js App Router, layout.tsx files nest automatically by directory: the root layout wraps every route, and deeper layouts (like the dashboard shell) wrap only their subtree. This is convention-over-imports routing — the framework, not import statements, wires pages together.

tour.title: The Request Gatekeeper
tour.description: Before any page or API route runs, every request passes through src/proxy.ts — the Next.js middleware entry point. It applies security headers, enforces same-origin CSRF checks on mutating calls, and can flip the app into a cutover freeze. This is the platform's first line of defense and explains the security posture you will see repeated at every layer (this is a GovCon/CMMC-oriented product). The headers helper it delegates to centralizes the CSP and hardening policy.

tour.title: Data Model and Database Client
tour.description: The Prisma schema is the canonical data model: 126 models and 70 enums covering organizations and auth, projects and boards, OKRs, RAID logs, finance, CRM, feedback, and the Foreman delivery tables — it is the single best map of what the product actually does. Every query in the app flows through the singleton Prisma client in src/lib/db/client.ts, which with 515 inbound dependencies is the most depended-upon file in the entire codebase.
tour.languageLesson: Prisma schemas declare models and relations in a DSL; `prisma generate` produces a fully typed client, and `prisma migrate` emits versioned SQL migration files. The client is cached on globalThis in development so Next.js hot reloads do not exhaust database connections — a standard pattern for Prisma + Next.js.

tour.title: Auth, RBAC, and Audit
tour.description: This cluster is the platform's authorization backbone and ranks 2nd through 5th in fan-in across the graph. session.ts resolves the current user from the session cookie and builds a per-org auth context; permissions.ts defines every permission as a BigInt bit flag with per-role masks; check.ts computes a member's effective mask and asserts required permissions; and audit.ts persists a structured audit trail for nearly every mutation. Every API route in Step 6 leans on all four, so understanding them now makes the rest of the codebase legible.
tour.languageLesson: BigInt bit flags let TypeScript represent hundreds of permissions in a single integer: each permission is 1n << position, roles are OR-ed masks, and a check is just (mask & required) === required — constant-time authorization with no table lookups.

tour.title: API Route Conventions
tour.description: All server functionality is exposed as App Router REST routes under src/app/api/v1/orgs/[orgId]/..., so every URL is org-scoped by construction — the heart of multi-tenancy. api-helpers.ts (313 dependents) standardizes the pattern: JSON responders plus a centralized handleApiError that maps domain errors to 403/404/409 responses. The work-items and boards routes are representative examples: authenticate via Step 5's session, assert RBAC, query via Step 4's Prisma client, audit, respond. Once you have read one route, you can read all ~200 of them.

tour.title: Multi-Tenant Dashboard Shell
tour.description: On the page side, the (dashboard) route group's layout is the authenticated shell: it loads the current user, org memberships, and per-org enabled modules/plugins before rendering any child page. The [orgSlug] segment resolves which tenant you are in, and the project layout below it resolves the project by key — mirroring in the UI the same org-then-project scoping the API enforces in Step 6. This is where role- and module-based navigation gets composed.

tour.title: UI System and Client Data Layer
tour.description: Client components share a small, heavily reused toolkit. The cn() helper and the design-system primitives in src/components/ui (button.tsx alone has 142 dependents) come from the shadcn/@base-ui pattern. On the data side, json-fetcher.ts wraps fetch with typed errors for React Query, use-org-mutation.ts auto-invalidates org-scoped query keys after writes, and types/models.ts holds the client-side model definitions that mirror the Prisma schema from Step 4. These five files define the idioms used by essentially every feature component.
tour.languageLesson: React Query's cache is keyed by hierarchical query keys; scoping every key by orgId means a mutation can invalidate just that tenant's data. Throwing a typed FetchError from the fetcher (instead of returning it) is what lets React Query drive retries and error states uniformly.

tour.title: Boards and Work Items
tour.description: Now the core product surface. The Kanban board and Backlog view are two of the six board renderings over the same work-item data, and issues-view.tsx and card-detail-sheet.tsx are the highest fan-out feature components in the graph — the detail sheet alone composes 32 modules to edit a single work item (fields, comments, links, dependencies, activity). Notice how they consume the Step 8 idioms: json-fetcher hooks for reads, use-org-mutation for writes, and ui primitives throughout. Board choreography (Backlog → To-do → In progress → Review → Done) is also the state machine the Foreman daemon drives in Step 11.

tour.title: Feedback Portal to Backlog
tour.description: This is stage one of the README's headline pipeline. The in-app feedback portal lets any user file feature requests and bug reports; the org-scoped feedback API stores and manages them; and the remediate endpoint is where automation enters — an hourly GitHub Actions workflow POSTs to it, triggering Claude-powered triage that classifies feedback and delivers it into the target project's backlog from Step 9. Human capture, scheduled machine triage.

tour.title: AI Engine and the Foreman Daemon
tour.description: The AI subsystem in src/lib/ai powers both the in-app assistant and autonomous delivery. agent-loop.ts is the unified tool-use loop; tools.ts registers ~90 native tools spanning work items, OKRs, finance, and CRM; and tool-executor.ts parses the model's tool calls and dispatches them to domain executors — always through the same RBAC and audit layers from Step 5, so the AI has no privileged path. The autonomous-delivery runbook then documents Foreman, the host-side daemon that works the backlog: isolated branch per ticket, checks, an adversarial reviewer agent, then PR, auto-merge, signed release, and deploy — or a parked draft PR for risky changes.

tour.title: Containerization and Deployment
tour.description: The Dockerfile packages the app as a multi-stage build — deps installs packages, build runs prisma generate and next build, and separate migrate and runtime stages run as a non-root user with only the Next.js standalone output. docker-compose.yml orchestrates the full in-boundary stack: pgvector Postgres with pgBackRest backups, TLS-bootstrapped MinIO object storage, a one-shot Prisma migration runner, and optional observability and OAuth-broker profiles. The Helm values file shows the same system deployed to Kubernetes with digest-pinned, hardened defaults for air-gapped and DoD postures.
tour.languageLesson: Multi-stage Docker builds use multiple FROM statements so dev dependencies never reach production; a dedicated migrate stage lets orchestrators run schema migrations as a one-shot job before the app starts. Compose 'profiles' make optional service groups (observability, Nango) opt-in within one file.

tour.title: CI/CD, Security Gates, and Release
tour.description: The capstone: how code ships. ci.yml gates every push and PR with type-checks, lint, and unit plus DB-integration tests; security.yml runs the CMMC L2 / NIST 800-171 scanning gates; and release.yml builds signed multi-arch images to GHCR on v* tags — the same signed images the Foreman pipeline from Step 11 deploys and health-gates. package.json is the single source of truth for the running version (v2.x SemVer), tying the release automation back to the conventions you read in AGENTS.md at Step 1.
tour.languageLesson: GitHub Actions workflows trigger via 'on' (push, pull_request, schedule, tags); separating CI, security, and release into distinct workflows lets each run on its own trigger and permissions scope. Tag-triggered release jobs ('v*') are how SemVer tags become immutable, signed container artifacts.
